articles.title: NBA Power Rankings: Early title favorites, rising contenders and relegation zone candidates
articles.summary: Here's how all 30 teams rank nearly two weeks into the NBA season.
articles.body:
Nearly two weeks into the NBA season, who has the best shot to win it all? I'll answer that question at the start of every month this season with my NBA Power Rankings here on Yahoo Sports.

I've ranked all 30 teams in the order I'd pick them to win the title while also accounting for recent performance. That means the undefeated Grizzlies don't rank first, but it does mean they've taken a big jump from where they were in the preseason. Let's get to it starting with the league's worst teams:

The Kings are winless. They didn't even win a preseason game. They've gotten pounded every single night and have very little hope of winning more than one or two of their next 13 games, which means breaking the NBA's worst losing streak to begin a season (0-18) is certainly on the table for Sacramento.

For Kings fans to stay sane this year, they can't be worried about the score at the final buzzer. It has to be about the development of rookie point guard Darius Acuff. Straight out of the gates, Acuff is averaging 26.3 points per game, but he's doing it on 24 shots per game. Over the course of the year, Kings fans should obviously root for more epic scoring performances from their rookie guard, but they also need to see him improve his scoring efficiency, develop as a playmaker, and show some heart as a defender. Acuff needs to prove he can be somebody who can impact winning. Or else he's going to earn a reputation: Empty stats scorer.

New Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins needs to pull the plug on the veterans. Myles Turner looks like he's coasting until he's traded. Tyler Herro ball watches all game long on defense. Kyle Kuzma seems more interested in podcasting and posting online. Why is Jenkins so invested in them? Every other player on this roster is under 30 years old, and has lots to build toward. Kel'el Ware should be fully empowered ahead of Turner, and rookies Brayden Burries and Nate Ament have both shown more than enough flashes to warrant more minutes. Let's see what these kids have.

What matters most to the Clippers this season is the development of rookie point guard Keaton Wagler, and so far you've got to love the way he's just hurtling himself into the paint. All that experience will pay off for him.

But everybody else around the league is watching for Brook Lopez, Derrick Jones, Rui Hachimura, and Kris Dunn. The Clippers have individually talented players who could help contenders around the NBA, so there is a chance they will be able to restore some of the draft picks lost from the Aspiration punishment.

"I'm 20 and I've never been a loser in my whole life so I'm going to try my best to make sure that doesn't happen, and I'm not ever going to accept being a loser," Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson said on Friday. "This is my job to be a leader on this team and it's all going to start with me, I know that. It's partially my fault that we started off the way we did, whether I'm the youngest on the team or not. I take ownership for that and it won't happen again."

If you're a Bulls fan, you have got to love those words from Wilson. He plays with contagious energy and enthusiasm, and he's shown major star flashes ever since he was drafted. But I'm worried the trio of Wilson, Matas Buzelis, and Josh Giddey is simply fundamentally flawed. None of them are pure point guards. None of them are knockdown shooters. And with Wilson being empowered as the guy, both Buzelis and Giddey have struggled to continue progressing in the ways they showed last season. Maybe they figure it out. But so far, it's leading to more losses than expected.

You have to find silver linings when you're watching a bad basketball team, and I hope Nets fans are enjoying the Nolan Traoré experience. It feels like you're watching a game at 1.5x speed when he has the ball, which allows him to create advantages for his team that a lot of guards can't.

The most encouraging thing about Sunday's 16-point outing was the fact he was hitting his spot-up 3-pointers. Shooting was the concern for Traoré entering the NBA, but now he's at 39% on this young season after going 4-for-8 in Brooklyn's first win. His mechanics look pure — he was even no-dipping on his 3s. If he keeps it up, the Nets very well might have their point guard of the future.

We're working with the tiniest of sample sizes at this early point of the season. But the Pelicans have a +19.2 net rating in minutes with Herb Jones on the floor and a -14.5 net rating without him. He played under 20 minutes in their first three games, and the Pelicans went 0-3. He played over 25 in each of the last two, and the Pelicans won both. If the Pelicans still can't score at an elite level — in large part due to a lack of shooting across this roster — then they should lean into playing the best defense they can. And that means Jamahl Mosley needs to put Herb on the floor as much as possible.

A few weeks before the season, Krysyan Edler was nice enough to interview me about the Jazz for The Deseret News. She quoted me saying: "I just don't see how this team is bad again. I just think they have too many good players, both young and proven."

I wish those words were totally fabricated, but I totally said that. I bought the hype that the Jazz would be a great story this season. And so far, it's looking like I was dead wrong. Jaren Jackson Jr. is already sidelined with a torn MCL. Jusuf Nurkić hasn't played a game yet. Lauri Markkanen looks like a shell of his former self. And all the young guys haven't been anything special. Darryn Peterson has been the worst of the top four picks. Ace Bailey and Keyonte George look like they've plateaued. Maybe Will Hardy actually isn't any good as a coach? Once again, the Jazz appear to be headed for the NBA Draft Lottery.

NBA reporter Chris Haynes recently said "there's some growing frustration" in the Suns' locker room because the roster "does not have a point guard that can organize that offense." Umm. Have the players in that locker room forgotten about Collin Gillespie?

Look, Gillespie is no Chris Paul. But he started 58 games last year, posted a 2.9 assist-to-turnover ratio, and vibed well with Devin Booker. This season, Gillespie has been moved to the bench in favor of Jalen Green, who is a black hole offensively. It makes zero sense. The Suns are posting a 110.2 offensive rating in the 92 minutes that Booker and Green have shared the floor. That number is 128.3 in the 43 minutes Booker has shared the floor with Gillespie without Green. Maybe, just maybe, the Suns should do a lot more of that.

How soon is too soon to worry about Franz Wagner's jumper? Wagner has made only six of his 31 triples this season (19.4%) and mechanically his shot looks completely broken with 67 moving parts happening all at once from the moment he catches the ball. Wagner is in the sixth season of his career and still hasn't been able to translate his soft touch from the line (85%) and floater range (nearly 50%) to the perimeter. He's at 32.1% for his career. But it's never been as bad as now.

Paolo Banchero's absence is also really felt since he can catch fire from the perimeter, covering for Wagner's primary weakness. The Magic are badly missing him, and until he returns it's hard to feel much confidence in this team. But Banchero is streaky himself, and his averages really aren't any better since he also goes through severe cold stretches. We might just be finding out that Wagner and Banchero aren't compatible.

Tyrese Haliburton returned to the floor and immediately looked like Tyrese Haliburton. But he's already sidelined by a hamstring issue, and now the Pacers already look like the same 19-win Haliburtonless team from last year. Indiana is being outscored by 8.7 points per 100 possessions in the minutes without Haliburton this season. For as long as he's gone, it's not looking like it'll get any better.

The bullish case for Atlanta this year was largely dependent on Jalen Johnson taking another step forward as a player. He averaged 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 7.9 assists last year, earning himself a spot on an All-NBA team. It's been a step back this year. He's not scoring with as much efficiency, his volume is down, and the rest of the roster isn't making up for it.

The Hawks aren't shooting 3s well. Nickeil Alexander-Walker remains more of an off-ball talent. And CJ McCollum is playing like he's 35 years old. If Johnson doesn't take another step forward, it's unlikely anyone else on this team will.

I'm having a hard time judging the Hornets, given the fact that both Kon Knueppel and Coby White have yet to play this season (White will make his debut on Monday). It doesn't seem fair to make any assumptions about what this roster is supposed to perform like without two of its three best players.

But it's undeniably encouraging that the Hornets have managed to pull off three wins and competed against both the Pistons and Sixers despite having a depleted roster. Once this team is whole, hopefully Brandon Miller's scoring efficiency can improve, and the rotation will fall into its intended place.

So much for all the talk about AJ Dybantsa not being an impactful defensive player. In his second game with the Wizards, he had seven rebounds and five deflections. Both Brandon Miller and Naz Reid had a hard time creating quality shots against him. Dybantsa moved rapidly against Miller on the perimeter, and battled hard with Reid on multiple post-ups. We know Dybantsa can score and pass. But the fact he's already bringing it defensively is answering the biggest question about him.

Conversations about Portland this preseason were usually about Tom Dundon's ownership drama, the comebacks of Ja Morant and Damian Lillard, and what to expect from a new head coach in Micah Nori. But perhaps the best story on the team so far has been Deni Avdija, who continues getting better after his breakout last season. Deni is still driving to the basket with a relentless force, but he's also now shooting 3s better.

When I interviewed Deni to finish last season, I asked him about the struggles he experienced as a shooter last year — he made 31.8% of his 3s. "You're hurting me by saying those numbers," Avdija said sarcastically before continuing. "I know it's going to come back. I am going to keep putting in the work." He clearly has. So far this year, he's up to 37.5% on all 3s and over 40% on catch-and-shoot 3s. Given the fact that he's going to be sharing the court with other guards all year long, it's especially important that he can space the floor to take another leap as an All-Star.

Isn't it such a blessing that Steph Curry still looks like Steph Curry on the basketball court? He's averaging 29 points per game on 69.1% true shooting, and the Warriors are still fun. But it's not at all Steph. It's rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who is helping turn what was supposed to be a grim year in Golden State into a beautiful one.

Lendeborg brings a versatile skill set to the floor with an inside-outside scoring game and a selfless passing gene that must make Steve Kerr have goosebumps. Lendeborg had 37 points on Sunday night and is averaging big numbers with 22.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. Lendeborg has been so good early on this season that it's hard not to wonder if he could even contend for an All-Star spot as a rookie. The last time that happened was in 2011 when Blake Griffin did it with the Clippers.

The Grizzlies remain the only undefeated team in the NBA, but they still are ranked outside the top 10 in these Power Rankings. Why? Largely because of the reason I stated in the introduction: I'm not overreacting to everything that happened in the first two weeks of the season. But also, let's just be honest: They have two wins against Utah, two wins against Sacramento, and wins against Portland and Golden State. Their next two opponents are New Orleans and Indiana. They might be 8-0 going into a three-game stretch against Oklahoma City, Toronto, and Denver. Those matchups will be better barometer tests for the young Grizzlies team.

But there's no denying how much reason for optimism there is. Ty Jerome has built on his strong end to last season . Cedric Coward has refound his 3-pointer, and Cam Boozer looks like he's going to be a multi-time All-Star for a decade-plus in the NBA. I predicted Memphis would hit the over this season. So in some regards, I'm not too surprised that they're looking good. But undefeated? With the best record in the league? We'll see if that can be sustained.

Is Cooper Flagg already a top-10 player at just 19 years old? This season we've watched Flagg lead Dallas to wins while outplaying Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Giannis Antetokounmpo, and he handed Houston its first loss behind a 33-point, 9-rebound, 6-assist effort. What we're seeing from Flagg right now follows a natural trajectory. He got way better after turning 18 years old at Duke. Then over the final 26 games of his rookie season, he averaged 25 points, 7 rebounds, and 5 assists. And so far this year, he's averaging 26.8 points, 6 rebounds, and 6.6 assists on elite scoring efficiency, an even better assist-to-turnover ratio, and more impactful defense.

What's this production gonna look like by the end of the season when so far he's clearly been one of the league's 5-to-10 best players? People will say I am being reactionary, but Flagg has been on this path for multiple years now. So no matter where he actually ranks today: Flagg has arrived.

The mysteriousness around Kawhi Leonard's health is the whole reason why it's very tough to pick this team to represent the East in the NBA Finals. Leonard might return midway through the year and look like a top player, just like he did last year with the Clippers. But who's to say he's going to make it to the finish line? Kawhi so rarely ever does.

So as much promise as there is in Toronto because of their youth and Scottie Barnes continuing to ascend, the Raptors are 3-3. And they're without their best player with no guarantees they'll ever have him when they need him most.

It's pretty crazy that Mario Hezonja looks like a better free-agent signing than Peyton Watson. But it's true. Through six games, Hezonja is playing hard, providing secondary scoring, and not turning the ball over. Meanwhile, Watson has made only 17% of his 3s, has offered very little in the shot creation department, and hasn't lived up to his billing as a defensive player. In a Cavs loss against the Sixers, Watson was unable to stay in front of Jaylen Brown down the stretch.

The Cavs have been solid to start the year, but they really need Watson to turn things around soon. He was their big-money, free-agent signing. Hezonja was a no-risk, minimum signing. But he's doing what he was signed to do, and he still can't do the things they need from Watson.

The Heat are still in the process of figuring out who they are. They started out 0-4, and they've won two in a row against Atlanta and Indiana. Head coach Erik Spoelstra already began to tweak the system against Atlanta. They ran 57 pick-and-rolls. Prior to that, their average per game was 23.5. Against Atlanta, Giannis had 24 screens, more than he did in the other four games combined. In Miami's next win against Indiana, the team set 37 on-ball screens. So the Heat are clearly experimenting between their innovative screenless system that we saw last year by integrating some more traditional pick-and-roll concepts.

The Heat kick off a five-game West Coast road trip starting Monday night in Los Angeles before returning home for a tough homestand against four contending teams. The next few weeks will tell us a lot about who this Heat team really is. And if it continues struggling, you can expect a free fall in the next edition of these Power Rankings.

After Nikola Jokić hyperextended his knee last season, his 3-pointer never came back once he returned to the court. Jokić shot 44% from 3 prior to the injury, comparable to his 42% clip the year prior. But after he returned, that number plummeted to 32% during the season, then 19% during the playoffs. Right now this season? Twenty-one percent. I wrote about the domino effect of Jokić's lost shot during the playoffs, and how that was hurting Jokić's formerly potent two-man action with Jamal Murray. The Minnesota defense was able to sag off Jokić, dare him to shoot, and take away driving lanes for Murray and everyone else.

The same thing is happening this year. When Jokić screens for Murray, the Nuggets are scoring 1.02 points per play. That's their lowest number since the 2019-20 season, back when people still questioned whether Jokić could even lead a championship team. If his jumper doesn't return, he may never again.

Look at Austin Reaves' stat line on paper, and you'll like what you see. He's averaging 23.1 points on 66.9% true shooting. But the Lakers are posting a dismal offensive rating of just 100 in the minutes Reaves is on the floor without Luka Dončić. That's down from 137.7 with both Reaves and Dončić and 112 with just Dončić.

The big question coming into this season was about whether the Lakers could survive defensively. They can't also have issues with their offense when their best player isn't on the floor. It needs to be resolved, or they may prove to not even be a fringe contender.

Houston is leading the NBA in offensive rating despite shooting the fifth-fewest amount of 3s. Oh, how times have changed from the days of James Harden when the Rockets were leading the league in 3s by an enormous margin. Now, the Rockets just favor quality. As a result, they are fourth in the NBA in 3-point percentage.

The Rockets won 52 games last year without Fred VanVleet and with Steven Adams missing the majority of the year. Adams still hasn't played this year, so head coach Ime Udoka hasn't been able to turn to his two-big lineup that inhales rebounds with Adams and Alperen Şengün. Once that layer is added to the Rockets, this team could look even more dynamic than it already does as one of the best teams in basketball early on this season.

If Victor Wembanyama doesn't reach the 65-game threshold, Ausar Thompson very well might be the Defensive Player of the Year. The Pistons have the best defensive rating in the NBA and they're 10.6 points better with Ausar on the floor — 97.8 with and 108.4 without.

But as much love as Thompson's defense routinely gets, I'm also intrigued by his offense. He still can't shoot. But the Pistons added enough other shooters on the team that they're now putting Thompson into a Draymond-like role in the post area, empowering him to spray the ball all around the floor. Ausar is averaging a career-high 5.2 assists this season. They're getting the most out of him, and they're at their best when he's in with his strange but awesome game.

It sounds ridiculous to say, but Jayson Tatum and Paul George look like they have more synergy on the court together than Tatum and Jaylen Brown ever did. Of course, Tatum and Brown won a championship together. Of course, durability is the whole concern about George. We'll see how long he can stay on the court. But Boston's vision for the Tatum-George pairing has been blatantly obvious so far this season. George simply accepts his secondary role and offers more complementary skills as a knockdown 3-point shooter and a superior defensive player. George is making 38.8% of his 3s this season, and he's second in the NBA with 5.5 deflections per game. Meanwhile, Tatum is posting All-NBA numbers once again with 28.3 points, 7.7 assists, and 6 boards.

I was extremely high on the Timberwolves entering this season, and I was having the most fun watching them of any team in basketball before Anthony Edwards was sidelined for at least two months thanks to knee surgery. It's scary now, especially because Rudy Gobert also looks like a shell of his former self as he deals with back spasms. The Timberwolves' defense has been horrific in non-Gobert minutes for years, so they have to deal with his issue while also navigating the offense without Ant.

All the talk ahead of this season was about how deep the league was this year, and how health would be the determining factor in seeding in each conference. Well, the Timberwolves went from a team in the conversation to compete for the top seed to one that will need to battle to stay out of the play-in before Ant can return. Gulp!

Are you worried, Knicks fans? I'm not. It's a slow start to the year for Jalen Brunson. OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges aren't hitting 3s yet. Mike Brown is still figuring out the best lineup combinations with this tweaked bench unit. It's a funky start for the defending champions, but they've played some really competitive games against some really tough teams in the East. Moving them down just one spot seems appropriate. If these struggles continue into December, then there might be something to seriously worry about.

One morning you can wake up as a fan and feel like your team is about to go on an epic revenge tour across the NBA all year long. The next day, it'll feel like you're experiencing a lost season without any guarantee of ever making it back to the championship. That's where Thunder fans are after losing Jalen Williams for likely the entire season and Chet Holmgren for a large chunk of the season. Oklahoma City is still built to win a lot of games this year. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is about to go ham. But the Thunder's hopes of winning a title again certainly took a big ding, given their injuries — Cason Wallace is also sidelined.

The absences also cast doubt over their future. Williams has effectively missed two straight seasons. It's very hard to get back to the level that you were at prior to missing so much time on the court. Holmgren has now played in only 56% of all possible games in his NBA career. Gilgeous-Alexander is about as durable, reliable, and consistent as any superstar. But his co-stars are the opposite.

After deciding to join the Sixers, LeBron James made it clear that Tyrese Maxey was the biggest draw. Maxey is certainly living up to the hype by averaging 29.6 points on 60.4% true shooting. He's an early Clutch Player of the Year candidate thanks to his late-game buckets across multiple wins, and Sixers fans are already hyping him up as an MVP candidate. Regardless of how this year progresses, it's been rather amazing to see his growth. He entered the NBA with such blazing speed but he knows how to better control it now, and his growing skill level as a scorer allows him to get buckets from any spot on the floor. The Sixers needed Maxey to keep ascending to be true contenders, and he certainly looks like he has.

Mitch Johnson's decision to start all three guards — De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, and Dylan Harper — came as somewhat of a surprise around the NBA. So far it's working. The Spurs have a 122.5 offensive rating and 96.6 defensive rating with those three on the floor in 66 minutes alongside Victor Wembanyama.

The three guards have, curiously, yet to play a single minute all together without Wemby, though. Instead, it's been one or two together, just like last year. But unlike last year, they've struggled. In every single lineup combination without Wembanyama on the floor, the Spurs have just a 105.9 offensive rating and a 123.5 defensive rating. It's no surprise their defense gets significantly worse. This happened last year too. But the offense didn't crater quite like this — it did by only 5.8. We're working with small samples, but the non-Wemby minutes are worth watching on the offensive end.

Nonetheless, this concern is a nitpick compared to the problems facing other contenders and the Spurs rightfully move to the top of the Power Rankings.

articles.title: LeBron James’ partnership with Mercedes Maybach reaches a new milestone as auction dates are announced for his Akron charity project
articles.summary: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has remained focused on his performance in the Philadelphia 76ers amid rumors of a potential retirement.
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has remained focused on his performance in the Philadelphia 76ers amid rumors of a potential retirement. While LeBron James remains busy with his career, it seems his collaboration with Mercedes Maybach has a new update as he remains committed to his hometown.LeBron James’ collaboration with Mercedes Maybach gets a new date for auction as his hometown in Akron is all set to benefitOver the last few months, the four time NBA champion LeBron James has continued to work closely with the luxurious Mercedes Maybach to create two custom cars. While one will be for his personal use, the other will be auctioned off and the proceeds will directly benefit his foundation’s I PROMISE School in Akron, Ohio.As per reports, the auction dates have been finally released as it is set for November 20 and 21, 2026, at the Javits Center, during the broader November 19–22 show via Gooding & Company at Rétromobile New York.A few days ago, Mercedes Maybach took to its social media to post, “The dual emblems say it all: @kingjames called the play, and Mercedes-Maybach brought it to life ✨ This exceptional Mercedes-Maybach S-Class will soon be offered at auction in support of the LeBron James Family Foundation. It's being showcased now until the 27th of September at Mercedes-Benz Studio Los Angeles.”The post added, “A one-of-a-kind story, made to make a difference. Mercedes-Maybach S 680 | Energieverbrauch kombiniert: 14,2‒13,2 l/100 km | CO₂-Emissionen kombiniert: 323‒300 g/km | CO₂-Klasse.”The two cars will feature a custom Light Ivory exterior with a contrasting black roof and a luxurious Stormy Weather blue Nappa leather interior with porcelain white stitching.Personalized touches are integrated throughout, including LeBron's signature crown logo replacing the standard V12 fender badges, his logo embroidered on the headrests, and the geographic coordinates of his hometown of Akron, Ohio, detailed on the center console alongside the birth dates of his children.LeBron James remains dedicated to helping improve more and more lives in Akron through his partnership with Mercedes MaybachThe four time NBA champion LeBron James has remained committed to his hometown, Akron, ever since he joined the league.All the proceeds from the sale of the second custom Mercedes Maybach car will be used directly for the LeBron James Family Foundation’s I PROMISE School.Ever since LeBron James joined the league in 2004, he has remained dedicated to helping more and more communities in Akron.The LeBron James Family Foundation’s I PROMISE School has worked consistently towards the students of Akron as they have continued to build new schools and provide accessible education to children coming from unstable backgrounds.For now, all eyes remain on LeBron James as he continues to remain a reliable athlete.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander drops season-high 43 points including dagger 3 to lead hobbled Thunder past Cavs
articles.summary: SGA put up a career-high 35 field goal attempts in what could be a sign of things to come for Oklahoma City.
articles.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had a poor shooting night and played without several of his top teammates Monday.

It did not matter. The two-time MVP scored a season-high 43 points including a late go-ahead 3 that iced a 117-112 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers. The win snapped a two-game losing streak as the Thunder continue to adjust to playing without several of their best players.

Starters Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace are all sidelined with long-term injuries. The Thunder also played Monday without Alex Caruso, who's nursing a sprained right ankle.

OKC still had Gilgeous-Alexander, and that was a enough alongside a makeshift starting lineup for victory over the Eastern Conference hopeful Cavaliers. Gilgeous-Alexander shot just 40% from the field. But he hit the shots when they mattered most, most notably a late 3 that gave the Thunder the lead for good.

With the game tied at 112-112 in the final minute, Gilgeous-Alexander gained just enough separation from his defender, Sam Merrill, to pull up for a 3 from the left wing. The shot sank through the net for a 3-point Thunder lead with 32.6 seconds remaining.

The Cavaliers didn't score again, and the Thunder secured the win to improve to 5-2.

After the game, Gilgeous-Alexander spoke with NBC about the Thunder adjusting in the face of injury adversity after entering the season on the short list of favorites to compete for an NBA title.

"Just figuring it out," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "You never know what the future has in store for you. All you can do is play the cards you're dealt."

Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 43 points, 8 assists, 3 rebounds and 2 steals. He shot 14 of 35 from the field, 11 of 12 from the line and 4 of 8 from 3.

The 35 shots tied a career high and could be indicative of things to come with Williams and Holmgren sidelined. The All-Star tandem have been OKC's second- and third-leading scorers behind Gilgeous-Alexander for the past three seasons.

Instead, it was Ajay Mitchell, Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams who joined Gilgeous-Alexander and Isaiah Hartenstein in the starting lineup Monday night. Mitchell finished second on the Thunder in scoring with 20 points and five rebounds, while Kenrich Williams add 12 points on 5-of-7 shooting.

It's OKC's trademark smothering defense that could suffer the most through injuries. Williams, Wallace, Holmgren and Caruso have all earned All-Defensive team selections in their careers and can't be replaced. The result Monday night was just seven turnovers committed by the Cavaliers.

But none of Cleveland's offensive stars broke out. Donovan Mitchell tied for the team lead with 17 points alongside 11 assists and five rebounds. Instead, it was a balanced team effort with seven players in double figures that kept the game close. A 58% (14 of 24) effort from the free-throw line ultimately doomed the Cavaliers.

The two teams will play each other again Wednesday night as they complete their season series in Oklahoma City and the Thunder continue to learn to play with a new-look lineup.

articles.title: Otro prodigio de Doncic, el mejor jugador de la NBA del momento
articles.standfirst: El esloveno vuelve a superar los 40 puntos para liderar a los Lakers ante los Heat
articles.summary: El esloveno vuelve a superar los 40 puntos para liderar a los Lakers ante los Heat
articles.body: No hay un jugador en toda la NBA que esté a la altura de Luka Doncic en este momento. Podemos debatir sobre si ha mejorado en defensa, sobre si su influencia es la mejor para un equipo que quiere ser campeón o si le queda mejor este u otro peinado. Va a seguir teniendo 'haters' como él dice. Pero es innegable que su estado de forma es el mejor de todos. Luka está por encima del resto y lo demuestra cada noche. De hecho, 24 horas después de lucirse con 45 puntos y 15 rebotes ante los Raptors, Luka casi calca esa gesta con un partido de 42 puntos y 13 rebotes ante los Miami Heat. Y lo más importante, el resultado de ambas exhibiciones dejaron el triunfo en el lado de los Lakers. ¿Alguien quiere más influencia en su equipo? Es pronto, claro, pero ya se habla de MVPs. Y ni Jokic ni Wembanyama ni Giannis ni Tatum ni nadie está a su nivel. Hacen grandes partidos, sí, pero Luka está encadenando uno tras otro. De hecho, ante los Heat, es la quinta vez de forma consecutiva que alcanza al menos 37 puntos. De esos cinco, en cuatro llegó a 40 y promedia 43,4 en ese tramo. Con el de Miami acumula 19 partidos con al menso 40 puntos, 10 asistencias y cinco triples, el que más en la historia de la NBA. Los Lakers, 6-2 en el arranque, empiezan a ilusionar en un Oeste que ha cambiado por culpa de las lesiones. Austin Reaves aportó 27 puntos y Walker Kessler volvió a brillar con 15 puntos y 15 rebotes, demostrando que, de momento, es el pívot ideal para el juego de Luka y L.A. En los Heat, que comienzan una gira de cinco partidos fuera con su quinta derrota en siete partidos, Giannis Antetokounpo aportó un casi triple-doble con 30 puntos, 12 rebotes y siete asistencias mientras que Klay Thompson hizo 19 y Bam Adebayo, 16. Doncic volvió a tener un dominante primer cuarto con 16 puntos (24 ante los Raptors). El mejor anotador de la temporada hasta ahora promedia 15 puntos en los cuartos iniciales de los partidos, anotando al menos 13 puntos en seis de los siete primeros periodos que ha jugado. Al descanso ya estaba en 24 y en el tercer cuarto hizo nueve más para acabar con cualquier intento de remontada de los Heat. Y un año más, como cada año que Miami visita Los Ángeles, Pat Riley se llevó una inmensa ovación cuando su imagen apareció en el marcador. Riley fue uno de los arquitectos de una de las mejores épocas en la historia de los Lakers y la NBA, el showtime de los 80. En L.A. nunca olvidan a su eterno 'The Godfather'.

articles.title: Baño de realidad en Houston de los Celtics del titular Hugo
articles.standfirst: Boston cae de forma clara ante uno de los favoritos en el Oeste
articles.summary: Boston cae de forma clara ante uno de los favoritos en el Oeste
articles.body: Los Celtics habían encadenado cinco victorias seguidas y empezaban a creer que estaban preparados para cotas mayores. Lo siguen estando, pero para tener garantías de cara a una posible lucha por el título, aún les queda mucho trabajo. Los Rockets se encargaron de recordarlo, 109-93 en la visita de los Celtics a Houston. Boston jugó sin Paul George (descanso), y Joe Mazzula repitió con Hugo González en el cinco titular. Es la segunda vez que el madrileño arranca el partido desde el inicio en lo que va de temporada. Esta vez jugó 16 minutos logrando seis puntos (3/6 en tiro), tres rebotes y un robo. Fue el titular con menos presencia en pista y se marchó con un -16 en el +/- del equipo. Esta vez tampoco brilló Jayson Tatum en los 'verdes'. Acabó con 19 puntos en una mala noche en el tiro: 5/16 y 1/7 en triples. Tras Tatum, 16 de Queta y 14 del suplente Garza, con cuatro triples. Los Celtics aguantaron el primer cuarto, 29-29, pero perdieron los tres siguientes. Los Rockets, que escalan hasta el primer puesto del Oeste con su triunfo y la derrota de los Grizzlies, tuvieron a Sengun como su principal baluarte con 26 puntos, 10 asistencias y siete rebotes. Jabari Smith y Amen Thompson aportaron 14 puntos y Kevin Durant hizo 12. Marcus Smart, ex de los Celtics, destacó con ocho puntos, cuatro rebotes y cuatro asistencias.

articles.title: Insólito: los Pacers jugaron sólo ¡con seis jugadores ante los Hawks!
articles.standfirst: Las lesiones están arrasando el comienzo de la Liga regular de la NBA
articles.summary: Las lesiones están arrasando el comienzo de la Liga regular de la NBA
articles.body: Es un hecho que las lesiones están cambiando el panorama de la NBA en este arranque. En el Oeste por ejemplo, aunque los Thunder están aguantando el tirón, las tres lesiones de larga duración de tres de sus titulares, dos para toda la temporada, les colocan con menos opciones de luchar por el anillo. Houston, por ejemplo, se ha colocado como la gran alternativa a los Spurs en esa conferencia. Y sólo llevamos dos semanas. Pero no sólo han sido los Thunder. Hay muchos equipos que ya echan de menos a muchos de sus jugadores incluso estrella de la Liga. Y los Indiana Pacers son uno de los más afectados, tanto que han protagonizado algo insólito en la NBA a estas alturas de calendario. Y es que, entre lesiones y descansos, obligados muchas veces, Rick Carlisle tan sólo dispuso de seis jugadores para medirse a los Atlanta Hawks en Indiana. En más de 80 años de historia, sólo una vez se recuerda una caso similar tan pronto, el de los Lakers de 1948 con cinco jugadores en su tercer partido de la temporada. No es la primera vez que un equipo juega con seis jugadores, claro. Ha habido varios casos en los últimos años, pero nunca tan cerca del inicio de la temporada. Es un caso más reservado a la cercanía del final de la Liga regular y el comienzo de los Playoffs. Aún así, los de Indiana hicieron sufrir a los de Georgia, 104-108, pero claro acabaron el partido sin fuerzas. El jugador que menos tiempo estuvo en pista fue Quenton Jackson, 35 minutos, y Kobe Brown, que fue suplente, jugó 38. La lista de bajas de los Pacers es inmensa: Tyrese Haliburton (isquiotibiales), Pascal Siakam (descanso), Johnny Furphy (rodilla), T.J. McConnell (isquiotibiales), Larry Nance Jr. (enfermedad), Andrew Nembhard (zona cervical), Aaron Nesmith (isquiotibiales), Ben Sheppard (rodilla), Obi Toppin (esguince lumbar) e Ivica Zubac (tobillo). Kelly Oubre Jr. fue baja de última hora debido a una contusión en la rodilla. Dicho de otra manera: la lista de bajas acumula casi 200 millones en sueldos, mientras que los seis jugadores que estuvieron en pista apenas llegan a los 15 millones. Los Pacers tuvieron que hacer frente a este partido con tres jugadores con contratos de doble vía, es decir, cuya carrera se desarrolla en la GLeague y a veces en la NBA: Braden Smith, Jalen Slawson y Kobe Brown. La de esta noche marca la primera vez que los Pacers juegan con seis jugadores un partido de la NBA desde el 20 de noviembre de 2004. Aquella fue la noche siguiente al 'Malice at the Palace' la monumental pelea entre Pacers y Pistons que acabó con numerosas expulsiones y sanciones.

articles.title: LeBron disfruta en Philadelphia y hasta ¡bebe vino en pleno partido!
articles.standfirst: Fue una de las jugadas curiosas de este arranque liguero
articles.summary: Fue una de las jugadas curiosas de este arranque liguero
articles.body: Hay múltiples signos de que LeBron James está disfrutando en Phildelphia. Están sus celebraciones, cada vez más raras y numerosas, su continua sonrisa, sus palabras, y su conexión con los jugadores importantes de la plantilla, especialmente con Maxey y Edgecombe. Todo va bien para LeBron en su aventura en Philly hasta ahora. Incluso lo deportivo. Siete victorias en ocho partidos con una aportación suya hasta ahora de 16,2 puntos, 7,1 rebotes y 7,3 asistencias, muy por encima de los 3,7 millones de dólares que cobra este año. Y los titulares logrando más del 76% de los puntos del equipo (102 de los 126 que le metieron a los Bulls para ganar). Todo marcha sobre ruedas. Tanto, que el jugador se permitió el lujo de dejar una de las imágenes más curiosos de lo que va de temporada. En una jugada producida en el tercer cuarto en la que sale por la línea de fondo hasta casi chocar con los aficionados a pie de pista, LeBron agarra el vaso del fan contra el que impactó y bebe un sorbo de vino ante la incredulidad y las carcajadas de la grada. Inmediatamente después, 'The King' volvió a ingresar en pista tras su 'travesura' para seguir jugando. James dijo una vez que parte del secreto de su eterna juventud es que bebe un vaso de vino al día: "Quería ver si valía la pena, si era bueno. Estuvo bien", dijo LeBron con una sonrisa preguntado por su acción al final del partido. El aficionado resultó ser Troy Clemons, que desde hace mucho tiempo cuenta con un abono de temporada de los Sixers y creció junto a los hijos de Julius Erving. Clemons comentó que no se sintió abrumado por el momento ni le molestó que James diera un sorbo de su vaso. Ni tampoco que le cayera vino encima tras ser casi arrollado por el jugador. James además del momento 'vino' tuvo otros también graciosos con gestos, bailes y celebraciones muchas veces junto a Maxey: "Este es un maratón muy largo. Si no encuentras formas de divertirte durante el camino, incluso mientras trabajas o estás totalmente concentrado, puede terminar agotándote", dijo James. "Nuestra afición es maravillosa, y nosotros intentamos corresponderles de la mejor manera: jugando como se debe, dándolo todo en el campo y, además, ofreciendo un buen espectáculo".

articles.title: LaMelo Ball, más rápido que nadie en la carrera de los triples en la NBA
articles.standfirst: Es el jugador que alcanza las 1.000 canastas de tres con menos partidos jugados
articles.summary: Es el jugador que alcanza las 1.000 canastas de tres con menos partidos jugados
articles.body: Cuando el 7 de enero de 2015 Stephen Curry alcanzaba los 1.000 triples en su partido 369 se dijo que era un récord que perduraría mucho tiempo. Y duró, aunque sólo siete años, cuando Buddy Hield, un 28 de febrero de 2021, utilizó sólo 350 partidos para alcanzar el hito. Ahora, ese tope de Hield, queda completamente pulverizado. De hecho, el anterior récord, 343 partidos de Duncan Robinson desde el 17 de marzo de 2024, ha quedado hecho añicos ante la gesta que LaMelo Ball acaba de firmar en un partido en el que alcanzó su tope personal de anotación de la temporada, 34, mientras guiaba a los Timberwolves al quinto triunfo de la temporada ante los Milwaukee Bucks, 112-100. LaMelo, que era duda por un golpe en la muñeca, acertó con seis triples en el partido. El tercero entra directamente en la historia porque es el 1.000 de su carrera. El jugador de los Wolves deja en 311 la cifra de partidos necesarios para conseguirlo, rebajando en 32 el tope anterior de Robinson. El de los Wolves es el jugador que más rápido ha acumulado esos 1.000 triples en la historia de la NBA. Ball se ha destapado como un tirador muy fiable a pesar de haber mostrado algunos problemas con esa suerte en distintas fases de su carrera. A sus 25 años ha logrado incorporar el lanzamiento de tres como un arma fundamental. Ahora, aunque no como obsesión, hay que ver si es capaz de amenazar el trono de Stephen Curry de máximo triplista de la NBA. El de los Warriors lleva 4.270 y contando. Son palabras mayores.

articles.summary: Hay jugadores que trascienden a la historia, y uno de ellos es Russell Westbrook. Se puede debatir sobre su juego, sobre si nunca fue un jugador capaz de hacer a un equipo campeón (sí finalista, en 2012), o si muchas veces jugaba para engordar sus estadísticas. Pero nadie puede dudar del impacto de este base en los equipos que ha estado, especialmente los Thunder, que el próximo 7 de febrero le harán el máximo homenaje posible.
articles.body: Hay jugadores que trascienden a la historia, y uno de ellos es Russell Westbrook. Se puede debatir sobre su juego, sobre si nunca fue un jugador capaz de hacer a un equipo campeón (sí finalista, en 2012), o si muchas veces jugaba para engordar sus estadísticas. Pero nadie puede dudar del impacto de este base en los equipos que ha estado, especialmente los Thunder, que el próximo 7 de febrero le harán el máximo homenaje posible. Oklahoma lo anunció este martes: ese día, coincidiendo con la visita de los campeones Knicks, su camiseta con el inconfundible número 0 se irá directamente al techo del Paycom Center para figurar allí como el segundo número retirado de la franquicia desde que se trasladó de Seattle, tras el 4 de Nick Collison. Días después de ese traslado, Russell Westbrook fue elegido con el número 4 en el Draft, la primera elección del equipo como Thunder. Allí jugó 11 de las 18 temporadas que ha estado en la NBA. Junto a Kevin Durant, que estaba un año ante cuando aún jugaban en Seattle, James Harden, que llegó en 2009, y Serge Ibaka, elegido en el mismo Draft que el base, lograron meterse en las Finales de 2012, perdiendo ante los Miami Heat, 4-1. La salida de Durant en 2016 no hizo más que acrecentar la figura de Westbrook, que el año siguiente se convirtió en el primer jugador que promediaba un triple-doble en la temporada (31,6 puntos, 10,7 rebotes y 10,4 asistencias) desde Oscar Robertson en 1962, y fue elegido MVP. Luego, Westbrook, aumentó la hazaña con otras dos temporadas más con triple-dobles, las últimas con los Thunder. Trss Oklahoma, en la carrera de Westbrook, estuvieron los Houston Rockets, los Washington Wizards, Los Angeles Lakers, Los Angeles Clippers, los Denver Nuggets y los Sacramento Kings, hasta su retirada al final de la temporada pasada. Sam Presti, vicepresidente ejecutivo y gerente general de los Thunder, fue el encargado de anunciar la ceremonia: "Muchos jugadores tienen un impacto, pero solo los grandes jugadores dejan un legado. El legado de Russell Westbrook se construyó tanto dentro de la cancha como en la comunidad", señaló Presti en un comunicado. "Su mentalidad era implacable y su compromiso, profundo. Por todas estas razones, los habitantes de Oklahoma lo consideran uno de los suyos, y su número será izado a lo más alto del pabellón en Oklahoma City para siempre".

articles.title: “I threw the cup in the trash”: Philadelphia 76ers fan reveals why he threw away wine cup LeBron James took a sip from
articles.summary: LeBron James chased a Tyrese Maxey pass into the stands in the third quarter on Monday, ran into a fan and drank some of his wine.
articles.body: LeBron James chased a Tyrese Maxey pass into the stands in the third quarter on Monday, ran into a fan and drank some of his wine. The Philadelphia 76ers beat the Chicago Bulls 126-107 at Xfinity Mobile Arena to move to 7-1, but the clip of James sipping a stranger’s drink became the night’s biggest talking point.The fan, Troy Clemons, has since said what happened to the cup. He told ESPN’s Kris Rhim he did not keep it. James had his own explanation after the game, and it came with a point about the length of the season.Why did a 76ers fan throw away the cup LeBron James drank from?The video spread fast on social media, and ESPN tracked down Clemons after the game. Clemons said the 41-year-old grabbed him after the collision and apologized. James took the cup, sipped from it, handed it back and ran onto the court. The spill did not bother Clemons. He said he was glad James is in Philadelphia and was just there to enjoy the game.“LeBron crashed into me; he grabbed me. He said, ‘My bad.’ My drink spilled everywhere,” Clemons said.The fan continued, He took my drink from me, and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back, and ran back on the field. I’m just glad for him to be here. I’m not worried about the wine getting on me. But I appreciate everything the Sixers is doing, and I’m here to have a good time, man. I appreciate it.”He said James is a man like anyone else, and a cup someone else drank from was not worth keeping. “I threw the cup in the trash,” he told Rhim. He then got himself another drink.Plenty of fans would have kept the cup as a souvenir. Clemons treated it like any other used cup.What did James say about the sip and the win over the Bulls?James said he had spilled some of the wine, so he wanted to know if it was worth it. His review was lukewarm. He also used the moment to talk about the grind of an 82-game season. It is a “long marathon,” he said, and players who never find ways to have fun will wear down. In year 24, he said, he enjoys the small moments and the fans who support the team.He once told former NBA coach Doc Rivers that wine is the only bad thing he puts in his body.The fun cost Philadelphia nothing on the floor. The 22-time All-Star finished with 15 points on 6-of-13 shooting, seven rebounds, nine assists and one steal. Most of his impact came as a passer. Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and Dean Wade all had success. James credited the defense. The Sixers held Chicago to few second-chance points, he said, which let them run.At 7-1, the 76ers are tied for the best record in the NBA.
