articles.title: New 2027 NBA Mock Draft As College Basketball Season Tips Off
articles.summary: College basketball gave scouts extra evaluation opportunities this year thanks to unusually strong preseason matchups.
articles.body:
College basketball gave scouts extra evaluation opportunities this year thanks to unusually strong preseason matchups.

First impressions have already changed or shaped some scouting minds.

While there is still some uncertainty regarding how the top of the 2027 board will play out, there does seem to be a clear No. 1 overall favorite.

It's also worth noting how NIL has changed draft projections, with the second round now made up almost entirely of seniors and international players. Sophomores and juniors without strong first-round assurances are returning to school for the financial security of guaranteed college earnings.

1. Sacramento Kings: Tyran Stokes (Kansas)

Position: SF/PF | Size: 6'8", 230 lbs | Age: 18

In a draft cycle lacking obvious star-level talent, rebuilding teams are counting on Tyran Stokes. His 6'8", 230-pound frame, creation flashes and shotmaking potential have popped for years. Questions about shooting consistency, decision-making and maturity have just kept scouts' confidence from rising to levels it's been at for recent No. 1 overall picks like AJ Dybantsa or Cooper Flagg.

Stokes ultimately passed his first big test with 27 points, eight rebounds and seven assists in a preseason game against Duke.

The early positive takeaways revolve around how he's been able to leverage his physicality and gravity. Strong yet fluid and shifty, Stokes clearly knows how to optimize his tools, put defenders in disadvantageous positions and draw fouls. His passing has also been highly encouraging, with Stokes showing the IQ to draw attention and see teammates, as well as the willingness to move the ball and act as a point-forward playmaker.

There is also more to be excited about than fear when it comes to Stokes' defense, based on his early movement and size for guarding wings and bigs.

It's reasonable to expect up-and-down shooting in the mid-to-long range. He does rely on contested shotmaking around the perimeter, and his high school percentages have never been super steady. Still, the self-creation signs are there, and he clearly has the skill level and confidence to connect on all of the various pull-ups and fallaways.

Unless Stokes' jumper really hits a wall, it's likely to be his professionalism, demeanor and impact on winning that determine whether scouts see the draft's surefire top pick.

2. Chicago Bulls: Jordan Smith Jr. (Arkansas)

Position: PG/SG | Size: 6'2", 205 lbs | Age: 19

There may be debate around Jordan Smith Jr.'s NBA ceiling, but he's still going to be very popular during a draft cycle lacking obvious stars.

Scouts figure to find themselves able to bank on his defensive pressure, given his strength, quickness, length and intensity. Offensively, he's going to shine in transition with his speed and athleticism, and while he may go through ups and downs with his shooting consistency and decision-making, Smith has demonstrated self-creation in the mid-range, three-level shotmaking ability and enough playmaking to be used as a primary ball-handler an offense can run through at different points of a game.

Inconsistent three-point shooting and 6'2" size are the likely drawbacks that cause scouts to hesitate projecting Smith top three in a draft.

3. Oklahoma City Thunder (via Clippers): Caleb Holt (Arizona)

Position: SG | Size: 6'5", 215 lbs | Age: 18

Caleb Holt's impact will be felt through versatility, which continues to expand as his creation and shooting keep improving.

Arizona figures to use him in a variety of ways from different spots, something NBA teams will value. Though Holt may not have one speciality skill, he'll find ways to produce with physical drives, spot-up threes, off-ball finishing, offensive rebounding, secondary playmaking and disruptive defense.

NBA teams may have trouble picturing upside, but Holt's floor should look high and fit will seem easy.

Why Tyran Stokes Tops Our 2027 NBA Mock Draft ⭐

Bruce Branch III has been trending upward for the past year with his on-ball development/creation and three-level shotmaking. But it was his passing that popped more than anything else during BYU's preseason. Branch looked like a natural playmaker during a pair of exhibition games, setting the table for teammates using smart pacing off the dribble, vision, timing and skilled, one-handed deliveries.

With Compton Magic last year, Branch also shot 50.0 percent on catch-and-shoot threes and 46.0 percent on two-point jumpers.

He should have AJ Dybantsa's 2025-26 featured role, good for allowing Branch to showcase his well-rounded skill set.

5. New Orleans Pelicans (via Bucks): Colben Landrew (Connecticut)

Position: SG/SF | Size: 6'6", 236 lbs | Age: 18

It looks like Colben Landrew could play a sizable role with a green light based on Connecticut's preseason.

He instantly stands out under the eye test with a 236-pound frame and rhythm behind his shooting stroke. There's also plenty of convincing high school tape of Landrew using his handle, strength and shotmaking versatility to score from three levels off drives and self-created jumpers.

He's set up to succeed with a point guard like Silas Demary Jr., teammates on the wing who'll draw top defenders and a coach willing to use freshmen.

6. Houston Rockets (via Nets): Stefan Joksimovic (Baskonia)

Position: SG/SF | Size: 6'7" | Age: 17 | Slovenia

Stefan Joksimovic crept into the top-five discussion over the summer after MVP showings at Eurocamp and the U18 European Championships.

The jumbo scoring/playmaking wing has always been an enticing archetype, and Joksimovic stands out with 6'7" size, a creative process, a strong shotmaking record and vertical pop at the rim.

His minutes and on-ball reps have been limited so far with Baskonia this season. But he just made three threes against Real Madrid, and he's regularly delivered assists that highlight passing IQ.

He does struggle to explode and finish in traffic, and it's difficult to feel confident about the way he moves defensively. Joksimovic could become polarizing if he continues to struggle to get clean shots off and find consistency from three.

7. Houston Rockets (via Suns): Patrick Ngongba II (Duke)

Position: C | Size: 6'11", 250 lbs | Age: 20

Patrick Ngongba II made strong first impressions during preseason, looking healthy, toned and more involved offensively.

His 28 points against Kansas were eye-opening, with Ngongba demonstrating a mix of post footwork, touch and shooting potential.

Adding a reliable three-ball would be a serious needle-mover for Ngongba, who flashed occasional range last season. His passing still separates him positionally—he can be a highly effective playmaking hub away from the basket. Despite limited creation to his game, offense can run through his IQ and knack for facilitating and hitting teammates in high-percentage spots.

Avoiding injuries, particularly to his feet/legs, will be key and help ease concerns over Ngongba's durability and history come draft time.

8. Indiana Pacers: Quentin Coleman (Illinois)

Position: PG/SG | Size: 6'4", 180 lbs | Age: 18

After a strong senior season, spring and summer showing with USA Basketball at the AmeriCup, Quentin Coleman carried the momentum into the preseason.

The hype continues to build around the growth of Coleman's game, which includes a well-rounded mix of shotmaking, creativity, explosive rim plays and a high motor.

He'll become more in demand by NBA scouts if he can demonstrate lead-guard skills as a ball-handler and playmaker, rather than project as a 180-pound combo guard who leans toward the 2.

Regardless, Coleman looks poised for a breakout year on a top team, offering an appealing blend of shooting, self-creation, athleticism and hustle plays.

9. Brooklyn Nets (via Knicks): JJ Andrews (Arkansas)

Position: SF | Size: 6'6", 225 lbs | Age: 18

JJ Andrews is going to give Arkansas physical two-point scoring, capable three-point shooting and strong tools for defending various archetypes.

Scouts will admire his 225-pound frame and developing perimeter skill, a combination that creates inside-out versatility and the ability to play/guard both forward positions.

Andrews should be an efficient, impact player in a presumed supporting role, while scouts should see his age and remain optimistic/patient over his on-ball development.

10. Atlanta Hawks (via Pelicans): Alijah Arenas (USC)

Position: SG | Size: 6'6", 199 lbs | Age: 19

There's no doubting Alijah Arenas' scoring prowess, which is fueled by positional size, ball-handling for creation and confident shotmaking. His efficiency will determine whether scouts see a future top option, instant-offense specialist or a ball-stopping, difficult isolation fit.

Scouts have sounded willing to give him a pass for last year's 34.1 field-goal percentage, which came after a late start to the season following a meniscus tear .

Arenas looked fluid and confident during preseason, when he showed glimpses of his footwork and improvisation working one-on-one.

Assuming his jumper falls at a better clip than last year, Arenas should become a far more efficient scorer by improving his decision-making, particularly around the basket, where he graded as one of the worst finishers in the country.

11. Orlando Magic: Miikka Muurinen (Arkansas)

Position: PF/C | Size: 7'0", 215 lbs | Age: 19 | Finland

Miikka Muurinen is going to generate highlights and excitement with explosive finishing and shotmaking for a 7-footer. He's likely to also stir up conversation around his maturity and decision-making, which have been questioned by both former coaches overseas and scouts.

Muurinen clearly possesses NBA physical talent and a coveted skill set for the position. Even if his three-point percentage underwhelms, he still has an easy-to-buy stroke and some ability to separate into pull-ups and fallaways.

Picking the right spots to attack offensively and avoiding emotional decision-making will be Muurinen's lottery ticket.

12. Miami Heat: Braylon Mullins (Connecticut)

Position: SG | Size: 6'6", 198 lbs | Age: 20

A regular name in 2026 first-round conversations, Braylon Mullins should be right back in the mix with a bigger role and easier path toward the 2027 lottery.

The historic shot he hit to beat Duke in the NCAA tournament highlighted his signature shooting range and shotmaking confidence. He was one of the most potent off-ball scoring freshmen, but he also possesses functional athletic ability for finishing and defending.

He should have a chance to be used in more ball-screen situations and expand his self-creation as a sophomore.

13. Memphis Grizzlies (via Timberwolves): Amari Allen (Alabama)

Position: SG/SF | Size: 6'6", 205 lbs | Age: 20

Amari Allen earned NBA interest last year with his ball-screen play, three-point shooting and 3.6 assists per game, a combination that highlights versatility scouts covet from a wing.

Between the 6'5" barefoot measurements, the self-creation limitations and inefficient results operating as a spot-up scorer, he just wasn't convincing enough during a deep 2026 draft.

Expected to become a focal point of Alabama's 2027 offense, Allen should be able to show more on-ball growth while building his shotmaking and decision-making reps. He's already an appealing 2-guard/wing prospect with how he gets downhill, hits threes and moves the ball.

14. Golden State Warriors: Ivan Kharchenkov (Arizona)

Position: SG/SF | Size: 6'7", 220 lbs | Age: 19 | Russia/Germany

Ivan Kharchenkov's versatility and defensive toughness should shine in a bigger role.

Even with the low three-point volume, he's a very likable prospect as a 6'7", 220-pound wing who can attack, handle and pass, finish plays, defend and make mid-range shots.

Kharchenkov has the chance to come off as a plug-and-play role player for NBA teams, especially if he's able to show improved shooting range.

15. Charlotte Hornets: Obinna Ekezie Jr. (Louisville)

Position: C | Size: 7'2", 240 lbs | Age: 18 | Nigeria

With Obinna Ekezie Jr. standing 7'2" with a 7'5" wingspan, any signs of outlier shooting or movement skills will generate NBA buzz.

His four three-pointers and five blocks in preseason against Kansas were eye-opening. Producing future lines similar to that one will undoubtedly result in Ekezie becoming one of the class' most coveted bigs.

Between the Players Era field in Las Vegas and Texas, Michigan and Kentucky on Louisville's non-conference schedule, Ekezie will have a lot of early chances to sell his NBA tools and offensive developmental progress.

16. Oklahoma City Thunder (via Nuggets): Abdou Toure (Arkansas)

Position: SG/SF | Size: 6'5", 200 lbs | Age: 18 | Guinea/USA

Abdou Toure's identity for Arkansas will revolve around his athleticism and motor for play-finishing and defense.

Continuing to show signs of improving ball-handling and shotmaking should help convince scouts to get in early on Toure.

It's easy to see Toure thriving in a two-way energizer role, but for a 6'5" guard, he'll become more of a return-to-school candidate if his creation and three-point shooting appear too limited.

17. San Antonio Spurs (via Hawks): Davis Fogle (Gonzaga)

Position: SF | Size: 6'7", 200 lbs | Age: 20

Off the bench, Davis Fogle flashed a well-rounded mix of on-ball creation, off-ball finishing, high-IQ passing, shotmaking potential and defensive playmaking.

With his scoring versatility and athleticism drawing attention in just 16.7 minutes per game, scouts will start to take Fogle seriously if he's able to replicate last year's production rates and efficiency in a larger role.

18. Los Angeles Clippers (via Raptors): Anthony Thompson (Ohio State)

Position: SF/PF | Size: 6'9", 215 lbs | Age: 18

There is a lot of preseason interest around Anthony Thompson with scouts looking to identify the higher-upside freshmen in this class.

At 6'9", he shot over 38.0 percent from three for both Western Reserve Academy and Indiana Elite. Ohio State will likely use him as a floor spacer who can pick and pop or roll, though he's flashed enough post skill and closeout attacking to offer secondary creation.

Between Thompson's shooting and face-up play, post scoring and 7'3" wingspan for finishing and defense, he figures to become one of the more popular freshmen among scouts, even if his production fluctuates. Thompson won't turn 19 until after Summer League.

19. Washington Wizards: Motiejus Krivas (Arizona)

Position: C | Size: 7'2", 260 lbs | Age: 21 | Lithuania

Motiejus Krivas would have gone in the first round in 2026, but he's now in position to become college basketball's most impactful big and a 2027 lottery pick.

NBA teams continue to show a high level of interest in massive defensive centers like Donovan Clingan, Zach Edey and Aday Mara. Krivas is next in line at 7'2", 260 pounds, a frame he uses to help shrink the rim he's protecting.

Though he won't be for everyone, teams looking for an immediate paint presence figure to view him as a long-term anchor.

20. Toronto Raptors (via Thunder): Na'jai Hines (Connecticut)

Position: C | Size: 6'11", 278 lbs | Age: 19

On a per-minute basis, no other player combined for better shot-blocking and offensive rebounding rates than Na'jai Hines.

Despite lacking any real creation or scoring skills beyond finishing and post-ups, his paint presence and defense are strong enough for scouts to look past the limited offensive versatility. He appeared to be in good shape and lighter on his feet during Connecticut's preseason, which could lead to more transition and easy baskets.

21. Phoenix Suns (via Cavaliers): Thomas Haugh (Florida)

Position: SF/PF | Size: 6'9", 215 lbs | Age: 23

For Thomas Haugh, a big NIL offer and chance to win a second national championship apparently outweighed the potential to go in the top 20 in 2026.

Even if he looks like the same player, lottery teams figure to remain interested in a 6'9" combo forward who's productive from three, explosive above the rim and brings sound passing IQ. Teams will value his easy fit and archetype over the potential upside.

Age figures to become a talking point, considering he'll turn 24 years old right after the 2027 draft. Still, we just saw the Golden State Warriors take Yaxel Lendeborg No. 11 after Michigan's title, and the certainty/translatability of Haugh's game could lead to similar viewpoints from NBA teams.

22. Charlotte Hornets (via Mavericks): Brandon McCoy Jr. (Michigan)

Position: PG/SG | Size: 6'5", 190 lbs | Age: 18

A torn ACL will cost Brandon McCoy Jr. his entire freshman season. It's going to create a difficult decision around May and June, because there's sure to be NBA interest in him, even if he never plays or works out.

Scouts have already had numerous opportunities over the years to scout and track McCoy, a disruptive defender, offensive playmaker and improving shooter. Missing the year may affect his draft-stock ceiling, but he could still look like an attractive buy-low candidate in the first round.

23. Oklahoma City Thunder (via Spurs): Jason Crowe Jr. (Missouri)

Position: SG | Size: 6'4", 190 lbs | Age: 18

Conversation around Jason Crowe Jr. will revolve around the translatability of his scoring and whether there's everyday playmaking potential to unlock.

The ability to create shots, make tough ones, shoot with range and take over games creates a microwave mode for Crowe. Shotmaking, separation tactics and touch distinguish Crowe from the class' other scoring guards.

NBA teams will just be asking how well he'll be able to execute his particular shot diet at 6'4", 190 pounds—or if he can switch to a point guard role and organize team offense.

24. Memphis Grizzlies (via Lakers): Deron Rippey Jr. (Duke)

Position: PG | Size: 6'3", 185 lbs | Age: 19

Even with Caleb Foster, Cayden Boozer and John Blackwell, coach Jon Scheyer should find regular minutes for Deron Rippey Jr.

The freshman moves differently, handling the ball in the open floor, navigating through half-court defenses and sliding his feet defensively. Rippey possesses the type of advantage-creating quickness and burst NBA teams value. And he's demonstrated an admirable balance between scoring and playmaking.

Rippey is listed at 6'3" 185 pounds, similar to 2026 top-10 picks Darius Acuff Jr. and Kingston Flemings. Given his defensive toughness, questions about size shouldn't mean much if he's able to show continued progress with his shooting and decision-making.

25. Portland Trail Blazers: Caleb Gaskins (Miami)

Position: SF/PF | Size: 6'8", 219 lbs | Age: 18

Caleb Gaskins should generate NBA interest with the ability to stretch the floor as a 4, operate as a 6'8", face-up wing and defend both forward positions.

Malik Reneau remaining eligible would make it tougher to build a strong one-and-done case, but the eye test should still detect an NBA prospect based on Gaskins' physical tools, shooting stroke and overall flashes of inside-out scoring versatility.

26. Detroit Pistons: Cole Cloer (Alabama)

Position: SF | Size: 6'8", 205 lbs | Age: 20

Cole Cloer should catch scouts' attention with an NBA-friendly mix of 6'8" wing size, shooting skills and passing IQ.

The eye test and track record suggest he's ready to immediately give Alabama a reliable three-point weapon. But he'll start to generate NBA buzz with more layered scoring fueled by clever moves, improvisation and athletic finishes.

27. Boston Celtics: Hugo Yimga-Moukouri (Nanterre 92)

Position: SF | Size: 6'8" | Age: 18 | France

Still 18 until after the draft, Hugo Yimga-Moukouri is producing in France's LNB Pro A for the second season. He's being used similarly compared to last year, operating as a spot-up scorer who poses a threat with his three-point stroke, slashing and finishing tools.

He's going to draw scouts to Nanterre's games regularly with the combination of 6'8" size and shotmaking that screams three-and-D potential. Age will buy him time with scouts who'll want to see more on-ball creation or passing.

28. Brooklyn Nets (via Rockets): Stefan Vaaks (Illinois)

Position: SG/SF | Size: 6'7", 215 lbs | Age: 21 | Estonia

After checking a coveted mix of boxes last year with 6'7" size, 91 threes and 3.2 assists, Stefan Vaaks should start the year on watch lists at Illinois.

Even with glaring athletic issues that limit his rim pressure and defense, Vaaks' shotmaking and passing are very convincing and fitting for an NBA connector role.

29. Philadelphia 76ers: Dash Daniels (SE Melbourne)

Position: PG/SG | Size: 6'5" | Age: 18 | Australia

Dash Daniels has looked far more confident and decisive this year. Through 11 games, he already has more threes and made floaters than he converted all season.

His shooting and touch are at a different level, important signs of a guard who lacks the handle and athleticism to blow by defenders or explode around the rim.

Daniels still looks more like a combo 2-guard than a lead playmaker. But if the improved shooting looks legitimate, he'll look more like a versatile, attractive guard prospect who can score in ball-screen situations, play off the ball and defend both backcourt positions.

30. Memphis Grizzlies: David Mirkovic (Illinois)

Position: PF | Size: 6'9", 250 lbs | Age: 20 | Montenegro

David Mirkovic's versatility is an obvious draw for NBA teams. At 6'9", 250 pounds, he proved to be an effective ball-screen playmaker with a handle and passing skill.

He made 57 threes and shot 39.6 percent on pick-and-pops, showing touch elsewhere on floaters/hooks (48.0 percent) and free throws (75.7 percent). And he brought down 8.0 rebounds per game using a strong frame and instincts.

Still, a total of two dunk attempts and low defensive playmaking rates highlight worrisome athletic limitations. And offseason foot surgery creates some uncertainty in terms of his readiness.

31. Utah Jazz (via Nuggets): Tounde Yessoufou (St. John's)

Position: SG/SF | Size: 6'5", 220 lbs | Age: 20 | Benin

NBA teams will love Tounde Yessoufou's physical tools, athleticism and motor for transition offense, finishing and defense. Because he totaled more turnovers than assists, there will be extra pressure on his shooting and ability to make threes with more consistency.

At St. John's with a stacked roster and a seasoned playmaker in Quinn Ellis, Yessoufou finds himself in a favorable situation to see more high-percentage looks off the ball.

32. Sacramento Kings (via Hornets): Luigi Suigo (Villanova)

Position: C | Size: 7'3", 289 lbs | Age: 19 | Italy

NBA teams were giving Luigi Suigo first-round looks a few months ago, particularly after he measured nearly 7'3" barefoot with a 9'6" reach.

He should be a focal point this year at Villanova with his combination of overwhelming size around the rim and developing skill. Last year with Mega, he registered a wild 15.0 offensive rebounding percentage and even flashed some shooting range with 18 made threes.

How well he's able to defend ball screens and opponents in space figures to play a key role in Suigo's draft stock, although he should remain a regular in the first-round discussion regardless.

33. Philadelphia 76ers (via Warriors): Cheickh Niang (Trento)

Position: SG | Size: 6'5" | Age: 18 | Italy

Cheickh Niang has stood out early by producing efficiently off his explosiveness, shiftiness and improving shotmaking.

Though still reliant on speed and bounce, he's flashed real promise creating with his handle, which is weaponized even more by how quickly he moves.

Niang remains raw at 18 years old, but his skill level is starting to show signs of catching up to his athleticism.

34. Portland Trail Blazers (via Timberwolves): Malachi Moreno (Kentucky)

Position: C | Size: 7'0", 250 lbs | Age: 20

A potential late first-rounder last June, Malachi Moreno returned to be Kentucky's defensive anchor and a more frequently used post player and playmaking hub.

His tools and instincts are selling points. In a more involved offensive role, showing improved skill level and touch could help ease concerns around whether he will be useful enough offensively at the next level. He shot below 50.0 percent on post-ups, pick-and-rolls and layups.

35. Washington Wizards (via Heat): Amare Bynum (Ohio State)

Position: PF | Size: 6'8", 245 lbs | Age: 19

Amare Bynum should start the season on breakout watch lists after his flashes of athletic finishing and three-point shooting.

He'll enter the draft discussion if he becomes more consistent from deep and a bigger threat to make plays off the bounce.

36. Utah Jazz (via Magic): Jordan Scott (Michigan State)

Position: SF | Size: 6'8", 200 lbs | Age: 19

Although Jordan Scott averaged just 5.8 points last year, his shooting and defensive tools still stood out in a reduced role. More shots and confidence could shine light on three-and-D potential, plus the driving and finishing ability for off-ball scoring.

37. Charlotte Hornets (via Pelicans): Nigel James Jr. (Marquette)

Position: PG | Size: 6'0", 185 lbs | Age: 20

Nigel James will have to battle size questions, but with his combination of strength and explosion, another jump in production and shooting could convince scouts to see an outlier.

He's already proven to be an advanced driver and finisher with true point-guard playmaking instincts. Raising that 1.3 made threes per game number could put him near 20-point-per-game territory while making him easier for scouts to bet on.

38. New York Knicks: Trey McKenney (Michigan)

Position: SF | Size: 6'4", 220 lbs | Age: 20

With Michigan losing three lottery picks, Trey McKenney should have the opportunities and freedom to emerge as the team's No. 1 option.

He's looked like a natural scorer since high school, combining a strong 220-pound frame with perimeter creation and shotmaking ability. His 39.1 percent shooting from three and 89.5 percent mark at the free-throw line underscore that scoring touch.

No signs of playmaking at either end (0.9 assists, 0.4 steals) suggest McKenney may be more of a specialist at the NBA level. But his positional strength and strong shooting indicators should be enough to draw NBA interest.

39. New Orleans Pelicans (via Pacers): Jeremy Fears Jr. (Michigan State)

Position: PG | Size: 6'2", 190 lbs | Age: 21

National Player of the Year feels within reach for Jeremy Fears Jr. after he averaged 15.2 points and registered the highest assist percentage on NCAA record.

Aside from demonstrating special playmaking feel, he also shot 42.0 percent on pull-up jumpers, a big jump from 26.4.

Still, for a 6'2" guard and limited athlete who struggles to generate rim pressure and finish, NBA teams will need to see a bigger jump with his three-point shooting.

40. Washington Wizards (via Suns): Alvaro Folgueiras (Louisville)

Position: PF | Size: 6'10", 230 lbs | Age: 21

More consistency from Alvaro Folgueiras should help illuminate the type of versatility scouts are often drawn to. At 6'10", he just made 36 threes, shot 71.4 percent at the rim and registered a 20.7 assist percentage.

The combination of finishing, shooting and passing for a power forward should attract scouts' attention, particularly if Louisville can emerge as a top-10 team throughout the season.

41. Washington Wizards (via Nets): Alex Condon (Florida)

Position: C | Size: 6'11", 236 lbs | Age: 22

Alex Condon has remained on NBA radars for the past two years with his athletic play-finishing, passing and skill flashes.

A non-shooting Condon should still draw second-round interest for an NBA team that values his ability to rack up 48 dunks and average 3.6 assists. He just becomes far more interesting with a three-point shot, something he's only teased scouts about potentially having.

42. Milwaukee Bucks: John Blackwell (Duke)

Position: SG | Size: 6'5", 205 lbs | Age: 21

After averaging 19.1 points at Wisconsin, John Blackwell is now a good candidate to become the top option and scoring lead for a national title contender.

He's an easy fit with his balanced mix of creation and off-ball shotmaking. Blackwell's lack of athleticism around the rim and playmaking will just prevent the NBA buzz from matching his college impact.

43. Indiana Pacers (via Jazz): Milan Momcilovic (Kentucky)

Position: SF | Size: 6'9", 220 lbs | Age: 22

Coming off one of the top three-point shooting seasons in history in terms of accuracy (48.7 percent) and volume (7.5 3PTA), Milan Momcilovic will again be auditioning for an NBA specialist role.

At 6'9", he shot over 45.0 percent from deep in the three major shooting departments: stationary catch-and-shoot threes, pull-up threes and movement threes off screens.

He'll get drafted to a team that values filling a need with a low-cost, sure thing over searching for upside or versatility.

44. Oklahoma City Thunder (via Bulls): Kayden Mingo (Baylor)

Position: PG | Size: 6'1", 195 lbs | Age: 19

Kayden Mingo may become a new priority on scouts' watch lists after he combined for 55 points against Florida and Illinois during preseason.

Though it's not a great time to be a small guard in the NBA draft discussion, he does compensate with a 195-pound frame and excellent floater touch.

Baylor's offense will run through his creativity that's fueled by downhill driving, shiftiness and improvisation. A 27.2 assist rate and 3.8 steal percentage highlight two-way playmaking to complement the scoring, though becoming a coveted 2027 prospect will still require Mingo to make a significant jump as a shooter.

45. Utah Jazz (via Clippers): Rueben Chinyelu (Florida)

Position: C | Size: 6'10", 265 lbs | Age: 23

Rueben Chinyelu learned how to use every inch of size and length, finishing last year as the Naismith Defensive Player of the Year and the nation's second-leading offensive rebounder.

He also improved his post game and free throws.

While Chinyelu's offensive limitations are well-documented, his tools, production and impact suggest it's worth picturing a plug-and-play finisher and shot-blocking presence.

46. Sacramento Kings: Billy Richmond III (Arkansas)

Position: SF | Size: 6'7", 205 lbs | Age: 20

Billy Richmond III is going to continue making positive plays off his athleticism, defense and motor.

Drawing serious NBA interest will mean hitting more threes—or convincing scouts that he can be a non-shooting outlier who adds enough value as a transition scorer, connective piece and defensive disruptor.

47. Atlanta Hawks: Bastien Grasshoff (Le Mans)

A productive start should have eyes shifting toward Bastien Grasshoff, a 6'6" guard/wing who's clever in pick-and-rolls and threatening around the perimeter. His positional size, craftiness and shotmaking flashes create appealing versatility, though inevitable concerns over his athleticism and defensive outlook will put extra pressure on Grasshoff's three-point shooting.

48. New York Knicks (via Wizards): Marc-Owen Fozdo Dada (ASVEL)

Marc-Owen Fozdo Dada is entering the draft conversation with tough baskets and defense in LNB Pro A and EuroLeague.

Quick and strong/physical, he's at his best getting downhill, putting pressure on the rim or creating playmaking chances.

Fozdo Dada needs to improve his shooting, but he's capable, and he'll still impact games elsewhere with breakdown ability and defensive activity.

49. Toronto Raptors: Kellen Thames (Saint Louis)

Position: SF | Size: 6'6", 210 lbs | Age: 23

Despite Kellen Thames never averaging 20 minutes or 10 points in any of his four seasons at Saint Louis, an outstanding physical and analytical profile could help him earn NBA looks.

Of the 15 players last year with an offensive box plus-minus over 5.0 and a DBPM over 4.0, one was Thames, one was Tyler Tanner and 12 were 2026 first-rounders.

Any signs of improved shooting will help, but NBA teams can start to picture an outlier who'll impact games with rim pressure, passing and defense.

50. San Antonio Spurs: Collin Chandler (BYU)

Position: SG | Size: 6'6", 205 lbs | Age: 22

Now at BYU, Collin Chandler should have a higher-usage role that highlights his athleticism and shotmaking while providing more ball-screen opportunities to create.

He's still not likely to sell teams on much creation, but Chandler can be potent in the open floor and behind the arc, a combination that could make him a potential bench-spark prospect for the next level.

51. Milwaukee Bucks (via Mavericks): Nolan Winter (Wisconsin)

Position: C | Size: 7'0", 235 lbs | Age: 20

NBA teams should picture a fit for Nolan Winter, who's 7'0" and shot 71.0 percent on rolls and 41.0 percent on pick-and-pops. He hit over 30 threes in consecutive years while demonstrating enough fluidity off the dribble to attack closeouts and after fake dribble handoffs.

Winter won't offer overwhelming rim protection, and he's had a tendency to fade or remain quiet. But he clearly has the size and skill set for a stretch 4/5 and screen-and-score big.

52. Chicago Bulls (via Cavaliers): Pryce Sandfort (Nebraska)

Position: SF | Size: 6'7", 215 lbs | Age: 22

With NIL bringing back underclassmen and leading to senior-heavy second rounds, Pryce Sandfort has become a name for scouts to track. He just averaged 18.1 points and finished third in the nation in three-pointers made.

Sandfort's shooting profile was elite and highlighted by a 45.0 percent mark on 80 off screen/movement threes. He should surface as a value pick with 6'7" size and shooting specialist potential.

53. New York Knicks (via Thunder): Amani Hansberry (Virginia Tech)

Position: PF | Size: 6'8", 240 lbs | Age: 22

NBA scouts could start to picture Amani Hansberry's game translating now that he's become a legitimate shooting threat, a plus-passer and solid interior finishing/rebounding presence.

54. Brooklyn Nets (via Lakers): Paulius Murauskas (Arizona State)

Position: PF | Size: 6'8", 235 lbs | Age: 22 | Lithuania

Paulius Murauskas put up 18.4 points per game last year, scoring with a balanced mix of post-ups, self-creation and off-ball play as a shotmaker and cutter. At 6'8", his scoring versatility continues to sharpen and expand, while his touch on floaters and free throws (84.0 percent) suggests he can continue to improve as a shooter.

55. Portland Trail Blazers: Arrinten Page (Providence)

Position: C | Size: 6'11", 245 lbs | Age: 21

Arrinten Page should become worth looking into with enough flashes and scoring production off pick-and-pops, post-ups, finishes and passing opportunities.

More consistency at Providence should help make Page feel more convincing as an NBA prospect.

56. Phoenix Suns (via Celtics): Finley Bizjack (West Virginia)

Position: SG | Size: 6'4", 190 lbs | Age: 21

There should be a regular attendance of scouts at West Virginia with Miles Sadler and Finley Bizjack in the backcourt. Bizjack's potential NBA appeal stems from his shotmaking versatility, scoring instincts and ability to generate offense from on and off the ball. His shooting touch, footwork and confidence give him a chance to carve out a role as a perimeter scoring specialist, though questions remain about his ability to consistently generate separation and finish against NBA size and athleticism.

57. Detroit Pistons: Somto Cyril (Miami)

Position: C | Size: 6'11", 260 lbs | Age: 21

Powerful at 260 pounds with a 7'7" wingspan and athletic leaping ability, Somto Cyril led the nation in dunks while registering a 10.6 block percentage. NBA teams should see a two-way weapon around the basket. He just had a turnover percentage three times his assist rate, and a career 54.1 free-throw percentage suggests it may be difficult to play him full-time minutes.

58. Philadelphia 76ers: Money Williams (Boston College)

Position: PG | Size: 6'4", 206 lbs | Age: 21

After averaging 20.6 points and 4.7 assists for Montana, Money Williams will have a chance to validate that production in the ACC. Limited athleticism and shooting range, plus 4.1 turnovers per game, kept any draft buzz from building around Williams last year. Scouts could still start to take Williams seriously if the creation and scoring craft translate this season against a stronger strength of schedule.

59. Miami Heat (via Rockets): Bukky Oboye (Auburn)

Position: C | Size: 7'1", 230 lbs | Age: 21

Bukky Oboye's 7'1" size and mobility for play-finishing and shot-blocking should attract more scouts' attention at Auburn. He just has to find a way to stay on the floor and dramatically reduce his 7.8 fouls per 40 minutes. In a limited role at Santa Clara, he still managed 58 dunks while shooting 77.3 percent inside the arc.

60. Charlotte Hornets (via Grizzlies): Andrej Stojakovic (Illinois)

Position: SF | Size: 6'7", 205 lbs | Age: 22 | Greece/Serbia

Andrej Stojakovic will need to show signs of improved shooting, but he was far more efficient last year creating and executing inside the arc. He's got the NBA wing size, scoring instincts and some impressive self-creation skill. A more reliable three-point shot should unlock three-level scoring that will make Stojakovic a more believable NBA prospect.

articles.title: 7 snap judgments from opening night of the men's college basketball season
articles.summary: UCLA is elite, Porter Moser is in trouble and other potential overreactions from the first big night of the men's college basketball season.
articles.body:
After an offseason of high-profile coaching changes, record-setting NIL deals and endless eligibility chaos, college basketball is, at last, back. Twenty of the teams in the men's AP Top 25 were in action on Monday night, including a pair of marquee games pitting ranked opponents against one-another.

Which teams pulled off opening-night surprises? Which suffered ominous losses? Here are some season-opening snap judgments after a loaded night of hoops.

Snap judgment: UCLA is poised for a big season

On opening night last season, Arizona upset reigning national champion Florida to signal that the Wildcats had gone overlooked as a potential conference and national title contender.

A year later, No. 22 UCLA pulled off a similar opening-night statement victory at Arizona's expense.

An 84-75 UCLA win silenced a pro-Arizona crowd in Las Vegas and underscored that the Bruins should not be discounted as a potential Big Ten or Final Four contender. This is, at minimum, the most talented roster that Mick Cronin has assembled at UCLA since the Bruins won 31 games in 2023.

The backcourt duo of returnee Trent Perry and Texas Tech transfer Jaylen Petty combined for 34 points and 12 assists and showcased the ability to shoot, drive or dish. Power forward Eric Dailey bullied his way to 13 points. Veteran center Xavier Booker was effective at both ends of the floor, while 17-year-old phenom Nikola Kusturica and fellow freshman Joe Philon III both displayed flashes of upside.

To beat its old Pac-12 nemesis, UCLA had to weather game-long foul trouble and overcome Arizona's three projected first-round picks. Promising wing Ivan Kharchenkov erupted for a career-high 38 points against the Bruins, but center Motiejus Krivas had a quiet eight points on four shots and heralded freshman Caleb Holt tallied just seven.

Krivas had the game's costliest turnover with Arizona within two in the final minute, thinking he had a teammate open for a 3-pointer and instead whipping a pass to a Wildcats player standing up on the bench. UCLA then put the game away on the ensuing possession, Kusturica going long with his inbound pass and hitting Dailey in stride for a dunk.

At the same time that UCLA football is enjoying an undefeated season, UCLA men's basketball could take an unbeaten record into December. The Bruins don't play another AP Top 25 opponent until facing Gonzaga in Anaheim on Dec. 5.

One thing is clear: Cronin likes this team.

As the notoriously cantankerous coach told CBS' Allie LaForce after the game, "I've not had a bad day coaching this team, and I know that's hard for everybody to believe."

Snap judgment: This could be the beginning of the end for Porter Moser

Porter Moser has spent most of his Oklahoma tenure on the NCAA tourney bubble, contending for a bid in four of his five seasons but making the field just a single time.

A second NCAA tournament berth feels farther away than ever after the Sooners suffered one of the most stunning upset losses in recent memory.

Oklahoma lost at home against East Texas A&M in a game that mostly wasn't even as close as its 68-64 final score. The cold-shooting, turnover-plagued Sooners trailed by nine at halftime and by 16 early in the second half before rallying to make the game competitive. Twice in the final five minutes, Oklahoma even managed to tie the score, but East Texas A&M answered to secure the program's first win over a power-conference opponent.

East Texas A&M is projected to finish dead last in the 12-team Southland Conference this season. The Lions closed as a 28.5-point underdog, making this the second-largest Division I upset by spread over the past 30 years, per ESPN research. The only bigger upset came when Eastern Illinois beat Iowa in 2022 as a 30.5-point underdog.

This is a pivotal season for Moser after Oklahoma raised more NIL money for him to assemble a more competitive roster. The Sooners don't have the tradition in men's basketball that they do in football, but they've reached Final Fours three times with three different coaches in the past four decades.

Yes, Oklahoma was missing standout guard Xzayvier Brown on Monday night, but that's no excuse for such a dreadful outcome. A fuming Moser acknowledged as much when he began his postgame news conference with an apology to Sooners fans.

"I apologize to every single person that came in," Moser said. "The things you do in a game like this in basketball to get you beat, we did."

Snap judgment: Did Illinois' offense, gulp, get even better?

Yes, Fairleigh Dickinson is coming off a 21-loss season. Yes, the Knights are projected to finish sixth in the lightweight Northeast Conference. Still, the record-setting 120-45 beatdown that No. 3 Illinois inflicted Monday night was a sight to behold.

Illinois led by 11 before Fairleigh Dickinson scored and by 19 before the Knights made a second basket. The Illini extended their advantage to 67-20 by halftime. The lead might have ballooned to 100-plus had Brad Underwood bothered to play any of his starters more than 24 minutes.

The craziest part of all is that Illinois did it all without star forward David Mirković, who helped lead the Illini to the Final Four last spring. The preseason All-American was already healing after an offseason foot injury and then also underwent an emergency appendectomy on Saturday.

With pick-and-roll maestro Keaton Wagler off to the NBA, Underwood has said that he intends to play faster than Illinois did last season but maintain a similar devastating efficiency. At full strength, the Illini will have five mainstays back from last year's 28-win team, along with an array of promising newcomers.

Snap judgment: Penny Hardaway has a chance to coach his way off the hot seat …

Interest in University of Memphis basketball was already waning with the program stuck in a second-tier conference and nearly two decades removed from its most recent Sweet 16 run. Then the Tigers bottomed out with a 13-19 campaign last season, one that might have cost head coach Penny Hardaway his job were he not the program's most beloved alumnus.

Hardaway overhauled his staff and restocked his roster with nine transfers this offseason, but as recently as last month the Tigers had sold fewer than 2,000 season tickets. They opened the season outside the top 75 in Ken Pomeroy's efficiency rankings. They were projected to finish second behind Wichita State in the American's preseason poll.

Could this season be Hardaway's last as head coach of his alma mater? Not so fast! Hardaway restored hope on Monday with a statement victory over an Iowa State team ranked 18th in the preseason AP poll and even higher than that in the major predictive metrics. Guard Jayden Reid took over late, scoring 11 of his game-high 26 points in the final three minutes to steady the Tigers and close out an 80-76 upset victory .

Memphis could have unraveled after Iowa State reeled off seven straight points to tie the score at 69. Instead the Tigers showed impressive resolve and leaned on Reid's ability to create offense late in the shot clock.

Is this victory an outlier? Or a sign that Memphis is poised to exceed expectations this season? We'll find out quickly. Up next for the Tigers: VCU, Vanderbilt and Louisville. And they'll have to play all those without center Nemanja Popović, who is suspended for the team's opening six games of the season.

Snap judgment: Iowa State isn't Top-25 good without injured guard Kilyan Toure

Take nothing away from Memphis, but this result is an early red flag that Iowa State didn't belong in the preseason top 20, let alone No. 6 in the KenPom rankings. The Cyclones were always in jeopardy of a big offensive dropoff after losing last year's stars Joshua Jefferson to the NBA and Milan Momcilovic to the transfer portal.

The shoulder injury suffered by sophomore guard Killyan Toure this summer was also a crippling blow. Toure is Iowa State's best perimeter defender and pro prospect. He's expected to be out until the start of conference play at the earliest.

Snap judgment: Gonzaga, at last, has a point guard

With incoming prospect Jack Kayil opting to stay in last June's NBA Draft and rising sophomore Mario Saint-Supery unexpectedly signing with a Spanish pro club a month later, Gonzaga began July with a glaring hole to fill.

The Zags were without a starting point guard at a time when top incoming freshmen were off the market and the transfer portal was no longer stocked with options.

Enter Xaivian Lee, the former Princeton and Florida guard once thought to have exhausted his college eligibility after completing his fourth season last spring and playing summer league with the Cleveland Cavaliers. Lee sued for an extra year of eligibility after the NCAA adopted a new rule granting players five years to play as many as five seasons. A California judge granted a preliminary injunction last month temporarily granting Lee eligibility.

Lee looked like a perfect fit for Gonzaga's free-flowing, uptempo system in Monday's 78-72 victory over Purdue . He scored an efficient 18 points on just seven shots and fueled an 11-2 second-half run that gave the Zags some much-needed breathing room. He also expertly took care of the ball and dished out three assists.

Most encouraging was Lee burying 3-of-4 attempts from behind the arc, an area of his game that floundered last season in Gainesville.

If Lee can stay eligible, he might be able to make a strength out of Gonzaga's biggest weakness.

Snap judgment: Thomas Haugh is worth every penny

Florida reportedly paid Thomas Haugh millions of dollars more to return for his senior year than the projected top-20 draft pick would have earned as an NBA rookie.

So far that looks like money well spent.

In a season-opening matchup between two of the nation's top frontcourts Monday night, Haugh was consistently the best player on the floor. The long, athletic 6-foot-9 forward tallied 19 points, 10 rebounds and 4 assists as preseason No. 1 Florida staved off No. 14 Miami's' upset bid and emerged with a hard-fought 77-67 neutral-court win .

Everything that NBA teams like about Haugh was on display on Monday as he carved up Miami without needing to dominate the basketball. He defended. He attacked closeouts. He sank catch-and-shoot 3s. He crashed the glass at both ends of the floor. He cut to the rim without the basketball. In short, he looked just like the preseason All-American he's supposed to be.

Miami will beat a lot of teams with bullyball this season.

That's just not the right formula against Haugh and Florida.

articles.title: Dillon Brooks Talks Fight With Draymond Green After Viral Video From Suns' Loss to Warriors
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks commented on the dust-up with Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green on Monday night that resulted in Green's ejection.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks commented on the dust-up with Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green on Monday night that resulted in Green's ejection.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Brooks said, "I was just trying to de-escalate it. He was just tweaking all game."

During the third quarter of Golden State's 116-113 win over Phoenix, Green hit the deck after contact from Suns center Khaman Maluach.

Green popped right back up to his feet, grabbed Maluach and threw him down to the court. Brooks ran in to confront Green, at which point Green grabbed Brooks by the jersey before getting pulled away.

Draymond was assessed a pair of technical fouls, resulting in his ejection from the game.

The Warriors were trailing by 10 points at the time of Green's ejection, but they rallied to win the game behind Stephen Curry's 34 points.

Curry suggested that Green helped inspire the comeback, telling reporters , "He lit a fire in all of us. We had to respond. I'm glad we did."

Golden State has now won five games in a row following an 0-3 start, while Phoenix is in the midst of a three-game losing streak, bringing its overall record to 1-4.

The Warriors and Suns are not scheduled to meet again until a few days after Christmas on Dec. 28.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball bought a $2.2 million Charlotte luxury condo in 2023, and now the NBA star is seeking $2.6 million for the 3,500-square-foot property, targeting a $400,000 gain
articles.summary: LaMelo Ball has put a Charlotte condo on the market.
articles.body: LaMelo Ball has put a Charlotte condo on the market. The Timberwolves guard is asking $2.6 million for the four-bedroom unit, which is $400,000 above the $2.2 million he paid in August 2023. The 3,495-square-foot home sits in The Trust, an Uptown building with only seven residences.The listing comes a few months after Minnesota acquired Ball in a four-team trade in July. Erika Mendoza of Coldwell Banker Realty has the sale, and the $2.6 million figure is an ask, not a sale price. Ball also owns the unit directly above, which is not listed.Why is LaMelo Ball selling his Charlotte condo for $2.6 million?The trade is the obvious backdrop. Minnesota landed LaMelo Ball and Josh Green in a four-team deal in July 2026, and the Hornets got former Sixth Man of the Year Naz Reid plus future draft assets. The 25-year-old guard had spent six seasons in Charlotte, which picked him third overall in 2020. He won Rookie of the Year in 2021 and made his first All-Star team a year later.The numbers tell the rest of the story. Ball bought the third-floor unit for $2.2 million in August 2023. The $2.6 million ask is $400,000 higher, and the final figure depends on what a buyer offers.Charlotte was a mixed run on the court. Ball played 72 games last season and averaged 20.1 points, 7.1 assists and 4.8 rebounds. The Hornets still fell short of a playoff spot, and Ball never reached the postseason there.Minnesota has paired Ball with Anthony Edwards, another member of the 2020 draft class, and coach Chris Finch likes the early returns. “He’s always in a great mood,” Finch said. In the home opener, a 117-94 win over Toronto, Ball scored 15 points, hit four of five threes and handed out eight assists. In Minnesota, Ball appears to go for a fresh start as a new chapter of his basketball begins.What features does the Charlotte condo have?The condo covers about 3,495 square feet as a corner unit with views of the Charlotte skyline. It has four bedrooms, four full bathrooms and a half bath.Polished marble floors with gold and gray veining run through the main rooms. High ceilings and large windows bring in plenty of daylight. The kitchen has modern cabinets, stainless-steel appliances and a big waterfall-style island, and the listing also points to wine storage and designer lighting. A custom wet bar handles the entertaining.The dressing room stands out most. Glass-front cabinets and built-in storage make it feel like a high-end fashion boutique, with space for clothes, shoes and accessories.Outdoor space comes in two forms. The unit has its own terrace with a kitchen setup and a dining area, and residents share a rooftop terrace overlooking the skyline. Two assigned spots in a secured garage are included.Where is The Trust in Charlotte?The Trust sits on South Tryon Street in Uptown. The building went up in 1967 and was later converted into upscale residences. With just seven private units, it offers more privacy than a large condo tower.Sports names pop up around the address. Michael Jordan, a former minority owner of the Hornets, also owns property there.The location puts the condo close to the financial district, restaurants and cultural venues. Bank of America Stadium, home of the Carolina Panthers, is nearby. So are Spectrum Center, the Hornets’ arena, and Truist Field, home of the Charlotte Knights.Does Ball own other property in Charlotte?Yes, one more unit in the same building, and it is not for sale. Ball first rented the unit directly above the listed condo from former Carolina Panthers quarterback Cam Newton. He later bought it for $2.47 million in May 2024 through an LLC, in an off-market deal. The unit had been listed at $2.5 million.Together, the two homes formed a two-level compound. Ball is reportedly keeping the upper unit for now.The upper unit cost $270,000 more than the condo now on the market. At $2.6 million, the listed condo would sell for $130,000 above what Ball paid for its upstairs neighbor.What is Ball’s net worth?According to Celebrity Net Worth, Ball has about $40 million net worth in 2026, with a salary near $35 million. Both are estimates built from public data, not reported figures.Much of the money traces to the five-year rookie max extension Ball signed with the Hornets in July 2023, a deal that could be worth as much as $260 million. Before the 2020 draft, Puma gave Ball a long-term shoe deal reported at $100 million. Ball was the only rookie in that class to land a major sneaker contract before the season began.On the court, Ball became the youngest player in NBA history to record a triple-double, at 19 years and 140 days. His best scoring year came in 2024-25, at 25.2 points a game, with a career-high 50 against Milwaukee. The site’s career-earnings tally reaches $241.5 million, a total that counts contract years still to come.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
The Miami Heat's sluggish start to the 2026-27 NBA season continued Monday as they lost 138-117 to the Los Angeles Lakers on the road.

Luka Dončić delivered a standout performance and flirted with a triple-double. Walker Kessler and Austin Reaves were pivotal in supporting roles.

For Miami, a double-double from Giannis Antetokounmpo and another strong showing from Klay Thompson provided encouragement. But that wasn't enough to make up for the Heat's porous defense.

The Lakers led by seven at the end of the first quarter and maintained that edge heading into halftime. The third quarter is where Los Angeles opened some breathing room. It outscored Miami 32-21 and then cruised in the fourth.

The Heat shot 50.7 percent from the field, and that's often good enough to secure a victory. However, the Lakers did them one better by going 57.3 percent overall. L.A. owned the paint, finishing plus-22 on points around the basket.

Miami didn't have an answer for Dončić. It didn't matter what Erik Spoelstra threw at him defensively.

Things aren't clicking for the Heat through the first few weeks. Antetokounmpo has at least made a seamless transition to his new team.

Spoelstra said after the game his squad had "no chance" Monday night because the defense was nonexistent:

The Lakers have a night off before they're back in action Wednesday against the Sacramento Kings. Five of their next six are on the road, so coach JJ Redick will have to manage the workloads of his top stars.

The Heat have four games left on their Western swing. They take on the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday, which is a great opportunity to rebuild some confidence.

articles.title: La plaga de lesiones del Real Madrid no cesa: Campazzo también cae
articles.standfirst: El base sufrió una lesión muscular en el partido ante el Recoletas Salud San Pablo Burgos y no jugará este miércoles ante el Panathianikos
articles.summary: El base sufrió una lesión muscular en el partido ante el Recoletas Salud San Pablo Burgos y no jugará este miércoles ante el Panathianikos
articles.body: Los problemas de lesiones siguen castigando al Real Madrid. Esta vez ha caído Facundo Campazzo, que sufre una dolencia muscular y, pendiente de evolución, se perderá algunos partidos. El propio entrenador del Real Madrid, Pedro Martínez, anunció que el base argentino será baja para el partido de Euroliga de este miércoles ante el Panathinaikos: "No contamos con él", dijo sobre el Facu y el partido ante el conjunto ateniense, "ni puedo darte plazos". Habrá que esperar al diagnóstico definitivo y la evolución para saber el periodo de baja del jugador. El base dejó el partido de este domingo ante el Recoletas Salud San Pablo Burgos en el tercer cuarto. Faltaban 3:14 para el final del periodo cuando dejó la pista para no volver a salir. Después del choque, Pedro Martínez desveló que el argentino no había terminado bien. "Ahora necesitamos a jugadores que antes, cuando no teníamos la lesión de Theo Maledon o la de Facu Campazzo ahora, no tenían la posibilidad de tener unos minutos que ahora sí van a tener", dijo el técnico al valorar la buena aportación de Max Shulga. La enfermería del Madrid no deja de recibir jugadores. Campazzo se suma a Theo Maledon (esguince en la rodilla derecha), Mikael Jantunen (rotura completa de la fascia plantar del pie izquierdo), Gabriel Deck (inestabilidad anterior en el hombro izquierdo) y Usman Garuba (rotura del tendón de Aquiles de la pierna izquierda). Nick Smith Jr., que estaba causando baja por una fascitis plantar, sí se ha recuperado y estará disponible para el choque contra el Panathinaikos. De una plantilla de 17, aunque con Garuba casi no se cuenta para esta temporada, Pedro Martínez sólo tiene 12 efectivos disponibles para los próximos encuentros, empezando por la complicada visita de este miércoles del Panathinaikos, que llega con uno de los equipos más potentes de Europa en cantidad y calidad. Dado el panorama, el Madrid otea el mercado en busca de algún refuerzo que pueda ya no sólo aportar sino aliviar la carga de minutos de quienes van a tener que jugar más por culpa de las lesiones de los compañeros. El técnico madridista ya dijo en rueda de prensa que el regreso de Eli John Ndiaye, cedido en el Asisa Joventut, era una posibilidad. Dispone de una cláusula de salida a partir del 15 de noviembre, pero ante las urgencias quizás se pueda acelerar su vuelta.

articles.title: Liberty reportedly fire head coach Chris DeMarco after 1 season, sweep in WNBA semifinals
articles.summary: Hiring a coach with NBA experience didn't work out for the Liberty, who played far below expectations this season.
articles.body:
The New York Liberty have fired head coach Chris DeMarco after just one season, according to ESPN.

The move comes shortly after the Liberty lost to the Atlanta Dream in the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs.

New York lost that series in a three-game sweep . The Liberty lost the final two games of the series by a combined five points, but had no answers for Atlanta's guard duo of Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada, in addition to Angel Reese emerging as a frontcourt star in her first postseason.

During DeMarco's lone season, New York finished with a worse record ( 26-18 ) compared to 2025 and entered the playoffs as the league's No. 8 seed despite a roster led by former MVPs Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones, along with four-time All-Star Sabrina Ionescu. (They could have had a fourth star in Satou Sabally, if not for a head injury that limited her to 13 games .)

The Liberty showed they were better than their regular-season record indicated with a first-round upset of the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx, becoming the first No. 8 seed in league history to defeat a No. 1 in a playoff series. Yet New York ultimately couldn't match a healthier Dream roster that pushed a faster pace of play.

DeMarco, 41, was hired after the Liberty did not renew the contract of Sandy Brondello four seasons into her tenure, and one year after New York won the WNBA championship.

Despite limping into the playoffs and suffering a first-round sweep against the Phoenix Mercury last year, Brondello was still the winningest coach in franchise history, posting two 32-8 seasons, two consecutive trips to the Finals and a league title. She also had the public support of Stewart and Ionescu.

That wasn't necessarily the case for DeMarco following the Liberty's loss to the Dream . When asked if the coach should return, both Jones and Ionescu said that wasn't their decision. Stewart echoed those sentiments, but then hinted at possible flaws in DeMarco's approach.

"I don't think we were consistent," Stewart said after being eliminated . "This is not cramming for a test. You gotta be ready to go and ready to go from the jump."

DeMarco also came under fire for the way the Liberty lost Game 2 of the semifinal series, failing to use a reset timeout in the waning seconds of overtime .

After parting with Brondello, Liberty general manager Jonathan Kolb reportedly sought a coach with NBA experience , such as Las Vegas Aces coach Becky Hammon and Nate Tibbetts of the Phoenix Mercury. DeMarco was an assistant for 14 years with the Golden State Warriors and also brought international experience as the coach for the Bahamas men's national team.

However, DeMarco had no WNBA coaching experience. Kolb might prefer to make sure that's on the résumé of the Liberty's next coach when looking at those who have been successful most recently.

articles.body: La jornada 10, cuyo arranque se adelante a este miércoles por un tema logístico, trae uno de los mejores partidos de Europa, un choque con aroma a Final Four y, quién sabe, si a a final de la próxima Euroliga en Abu Dabi. Real Madrid y Panathinaikos miden sus fuerzas en un Movistar Arena en el que hasta ahora no ha ganado nadie que no sea el equipo blanco. Llega a Madrid el Panathinaikos como líder de la Euroliga pero con dos derrotas en su casillero en sus dos últimos partidos. Uno fue en Estambul, ante el irregular Anadolu Efes, por un claro 83-68. El otro, más sorprendente todavía, el la Liga griega ante el Aris de Salónica, 101-91. Los 'verdes', muy sólidos en el arranque, han empezado a tener problemas en cuanto han viajado. Jugaron seis de sus siete primeros partidos de la Euroliga en el OAKA. En materia de enfermería, el equipo de Obradovic ha recuperado a una de sus grandes estrellas, Kendrick Nunn, y tiene principalmente las dudas de Kostas Sloukas y de Nikos Rogkavopoulos. Su plantilla es quizá la más potente de toda la Euroliga y es el gran favorito al título. El Madrid se ha ganado ser también considerado favorito tras recuperar, con seis triunfos seguidos, las tres derrotas iniciales que hicieron saltar las señales de alarma. Pero ahora se mueven entre los problemas por lesiones. En los últimos partidos han perdido a Jantunen, larga duración, a Maledon, para unas semanas y la última baja la de Facundo Campazzo con una lesión muscular que le impedirá estar disponible para Pedro Martínez al menos ante los griegos. Quien sí estará es Nick Smith Jr. recuperado de sus problemas, además de Olivier Sarr y Max Shulga que dieron un paso adelante en el partido ante el San Pablo Burgos de la Liga Endesa. El encuentro entre el Real Madrid - Panathinaikos, correspondiente a la décima jornada de la Euroliga, se disputa este miércoles 4 de noviembr a las 20.45 horas (horario peninsular español) en el Movistar Arena de Madrid. articles.title: Kendrick Perry ironiza con Conde y su arbitraje ante el Unicaja
articles.standfirst: Vidorreta y el club también están molestos
articles.summary: Vidorreta y el club también están molestos
articles.body: El Unicaja no está satisfecho con las actuaciones arbitrales de sus dos últimos compromisos en la Liga Endesa. Las derrotas ante el Real Madrid y el FC Barcelona, ambas decididas por diferencias mínimas, han dejado un importante malestar en el vestuario y en los despachos de Los Guindos. La coincidencia de Antonio Conde como árbitro principal en los dos encuentros también ha llamado la atención del club, que tiene previsto trasladar sus inquietudes a los responsables arbitrales de la ACB para solicitar explicaciones. El último episodio llegó en el encuentro frente al Barcelona, que terminó con victoria azulgrana por 89-92. Hubo varias decisiones que generaron protestas, aunque una de las que más indignación provocó se produjo con el marcador igualado. A falta de 2:03 para el final, Kalinoski recuperó un balón y terminó en el suelo para hacerse con la posesión. Punter se abalanzó sobre él y lo sujetó por detrás, sin llegar a tocar el balón. Los colegiados señalaron lucha y la flecha de alternancia favoreció al conjunto catalán. La decisión cambió el escenario de una jugada importante. El Unicaja pasó de tener la posibilidad de disponer de una posesión para ponerse por delante a ver cómo el Barcelona recuperaba el balón. La acción terminó con dos tiros libres anotados por Punter, exjugador del Partizan. En el banquillo malagueño tampoco sentaron bien otras decisiones del encuentro, como la técnica señalada a Txus Vidorreta después de reclamar una posible falta de Parra sobre Hunt. En el club consideran que el castigo fue excesivo, teniendo en cuenta que el técnico no había protagonizado protestas especialmente llamativas durante el partido. Perry también recibió una técnica. El enfado tiene un antecedente muy reciente. En la primera jornada de la competición, el Unicaja también acabó perjudicado por una decisión de lucha en los últimos segundos de su visita al Movistar Arena. Con los malagueños por delante (84-85) y apenas 53 segundos por jugarse, Amine Noua se hizo con el balón, pero Abalde y Deck acudieron a disputárselo. Los árbitros señalaron lucha y la posesión correspondió al Real Madrid por la alternancia. Aquella acción dio paso a un triple de Luwawu-Cabarrot que resultó determinante para que el conjunto blanco terminase llevándose el triunfo por dos puntos. Dos finales ajustados y dos decisiones de lucha que han alimentado el descontento en el equipo malagueño. La indignación también ha tenido reflejo en las redes sociales. Kendrick Perry publicó en su cuenta de X un GIF de Batman en actitud pensativa, acariciándose la barbilla. Un gesto irónico, pero que deja entrever que el malestar por lo sucedido en los últimos minutos de ambos encuentros no se limita al cuerpo técnico. El propio Vidorreta ya había expresado su sorpresa en la rueda de prensa posterior al partido contra el Barcelona. "Muchas situaciones que son extrañas; la designación en sí misma es extraña: que el mismo árbitro nos arbitre ante el Madrid y el Barcelona", señaló el entrenador.

Los estadounidenses están llamados a renovar toda la Cámara de Representantes y un tercio del Senado, además de elegir cargos estatales y locales. La competición deja libre la jornada electoral por cuarta vez en los últimos cinco años. La iniciativa comenzó en 2022 y se mantuvo en 2023 y 2024, antes de que la liga programara partidos en esa fecha en 2025. La NBA anunció la recuperación de esta medida al presentar el calendario de la temporada 2026-2027 y explicó que busca alentar a su comunidad a planificar su voto. Los 30 equipos tenían partidos programados este lunes, y la competición se reanudará el miércoles, 4 de noviembre, con 14 encuentros.

articles.title: 'It was all right': LeBron James takes a sip of fan's wine during Sixers' win over Bulls
articles.summary: One of the NBA's most well-known oenophiles broke new ground in the wine game on Monday: drinking it *during* the game.
articles.body:
Like many very rich people, 40-somethings and very rich 40-somethings, LeBron James loves himself some wine.

The all-time leading scorer in NBA history has long been nose-deep in the wine game, raising glasses with longtime pals-turned-oenophiles like Carmelo Anthony and Chris Paul for more than a decade. His Instagram posts about which wines he and his teammates were enjoying on any given night could drive consumption trends . He's appeared on the cover of Wine Enthusiast magazine ; he once pulled up to a Los Angeles Lakers game with a glass of wine . When he and eventual Lakers head coach JJ Redick launched their basketball strategy podcast, "Mind the Game," every discussion of coverages and tactics was punctuated by no small number of swirls and sips ; no less a source than r/wine has proclaimed the King "no wine slouch." (And Reddit would never steer you wrong.)

"I've heard it's good for the heart," James told ESPN's Baxter Holmes for a story on the NBA's "secret wine society" published in 2020. "Listen, I'm playing the best basketball of my life, and I'm drinking some wine pretty much every day. Whatever it is, I'll take it."

James isn't quite playing the best basketball of his life anymore, near the start of his 24th professional season and his first as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. He's still pretty damn good, though, and he's still taking it, whatever it is … even if "it" is in a fan's cup during a game.

With the Sixers holding an 11-point lead on the visiting Chicago Bulls in Philadelphia on Monday night, James leaked out in transition after a missed 3-pointer by Bulls swingman Isaac Okoro. After corralling the long rebound, Philly point guard Tyrese Maxey looked up and tossed a hit-ahead pass for the streaking James … that was just a bit too ambitious for the about-to-be-42-year-old to haul in.

As the ball went out of bounds, so too did James. As he did, he bumped into a fan seated several rows back behind the Sixers' basket. Rather than sprinting back onto the floor to get back on defense, though, LeBron lingered for a moment — long enough, in fact, for the referees to prevent the Bulls from inbounding the ball without him, and for Maxey to run after his new teammate to get him back into the game.

Soon afterward, the replays showed us why. LeBron didn't just take a moment to say hi to a fan; he also took a little swig of what the fan was sipping on, too.

"LeBron crashed into me," the fan, Troy Clemons, told ESPN's Kris Rhim . "He grabbed me, he said, 'My bad.' My drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me, and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the field."

"I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm, how good it was," a smiling James said in the locker room after the game, according to Rhim . "It was all right."

This isn't the first time that James has considered engaging in a bit of mid-game imbibing with fans. Back in 2017, with his Cleveland Cavaliers holding a lead over the Toronto Raptors in the first game of the second round of the playoffs, James found himself frustrated after smoking a layup that would've given him a chance for a three-point play … and expressed his emotions by skipping over to a courtside vendor and grabbing a bottle of beer out of her hand :

That time, though, James didn't actually slug it down.

"Not much of a beer guy," he said at the time. "If she had had some red wine, I probably would have definitely took a sip."

Even with how expensive drinks are at arenas these days, Clemons didn't much mind the spill — or sharing a little bit of his spirit with Philly's newest superstar.

"I'm just glad for him to be here," Clemons said . "I'm not worried about the wine getting on me."

Nor, for that matter, were the 76ers too worried about the Bulls. Philly controlled the action for the bulk of the contest, leading by as many as 22 points in what ended as a 126-107 win . Maxey led all scorers with 26 points and 11 rebounds in the win, which improved the Sixers to 7-1, good for first place in the Eastern Conference — a strong, and very enjoyable, start to the voyage for this new-look superteam.

"Listen, it's a long marathon," James said after the game . "If you don't find ways to have fun throughout it — even though you're working, even though you're locked in — then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career too, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments."

Clemons enjoyed the moment, too — although, somewhat shockingly, he didn't decide to commemorate it with what would've been a 1-of-1 collectible.

"At the end of the day he's another man like me," Clemons said, according to NBC Sports Philadelphia . "I mean, he's LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it's nothing up with him — I just got a fresh drink, though."
